info.name: Bifrost Provider Harness
info.description:
Smoke-test harness exercising every Bifrost provider surface.

Covers:
1. Native Bifrost API (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`).
2. Drop-in integrations: `/openai`, `/anthropic`, `/bedrock`, `/genai`, plus Azure (via `/openai/openai/deployments/...`) and Vertex (via `/genai`).
3. Criss-Cross matrix (§8): every drop-in request shape × every model provider × every supported modality (chat, streaming, embeddings, audio, image gen, tool calling, vision, JSON, reasoning). Cells where the provider doesn't support the modality are tagged `[SKIP]` and skipped at runtime unless `include_skip=1`.

Set the `baseUrl` and provider key variables before running. Run end-to-end with `make run-provider-harness-test` from the repo root. Run criss-cross only with `make run-provider-harness-test FOLDER="8. Criss-Cross"`.

exec: // Skip [PREVIEW]-tagged requests unless include_preview=1 (set via Newman --env-var include_preview=1).
// Use for account/region-scoped resources: preview models, vector stores, cached content, MCP servers.
// Skip [SKIP]-tagged requests unless include_skip=1 (set via Newman --env-var include_skip=1).
// Used in the criss-cross matrix (§8) to mark provider+modality cells that return NewUnsupportedOperationError by design (e.g., anthropic embeddings, bedrock audio).
// Per-request compat override: when compat is set (via Newman --env-var compat=true), inject the x-bf-compat header on every request.
// Absent => harness baseline (compat config off). Lets the suite run once with compat off and once with compat on.
// Prompt-caching harness (Round 31): stable per-run nonce so write/read pairs share a cold-then-warm prefix.
// Rows tagged [EXPECT-4XX] assert an upstream rejection instead of success. They exist
// where a dropped request field is otherwise unobservable: sending a deliberately
// invalid value and requiring the 4xx proves the field actually reached the provider,
// because a 2xx would mean Bifrost swallowed it. Same name-tag idiom as [PREVIEW]/[SKIP].
// Other requests require HTTP 200 unless tagged with an exact status, such as [EXPECT-202].
pm.test('Status code is 4xx (expected upstream rejection)', function () {
'; a 2xx means the field never reached the provider: ' + pm.response.text().slice(0, 300))
// Only register the content-shape test when the request actually succeeded.
// Otherwise newman reports it as passing (because of an early return) which is misleading next to a failing status.
// Management API (/api/...) and OAuth (/oauth2/...) responses carry no inference content, so the shape check does not apply to them; those rows assert their own bodies.
pm.test('Response has content (text or tool_use)', function () {
if (first > 0 && first < 0x20 && first !== 0x09 && first !== 0x0a && first !== 0x0d) { return; }
pm.expect.fail('response was not valid JSON: ' + e.message);
} else if (j.message && typeof j.message === 'object' && (j.message.content !== undefined || Array.isArray(j.message.tool_calls))) {

var cohereHasText = typeof cohereContent === 'string' ? cohereContent.length > 0 : Array.isArray(cohereContent) && cohereContent.some(function (c) { return c && ((c.type === 'text' && c.text) || (c.type === 'thinking' && c.thinking)); });
// Stop-sequence truncation can yield content:null with non-zero completion_tokens — treat as valid response.
if (!hasContent && j.choices[0].finish_reason === 'stop' && j.usage && j.usage.completion_tokens > 0) { hasContent = true; }

// finish_reason 'length' is the openai-shaped twin of the anthropic-messages stop_reason 'max_tokens' forgiveness below. A reasoning model can spend the whole max_tokens cap thinking and end the turn mid-thought, returning content:null alongside a populated reasoning/reasoning_content field. Tokens were produced and the gateway relayed exactly what the provider sent, so failing here reports a defect in whatever the row was actually measuring rather than anything that went wrong. An empty content with zero completion tokens is still a failure.
if (!hasContent && j.choices[0].finish_reason === 'length' && j.usage && j.usage.completion_tokens > 0) { hasContent = true; }
hasContent = j.content.some(function (c) { return c && (c.type === 'text' && c.text) || c.type === 'tool_use' || c.type === 'server_tool_use'; });

// Adaptive-thinking models spend output tokens on thinking before any visible block. Sonnet 5 is adaptive-only and rejects thinking:{type:'enabled'}, so there is no budget_tokens knob to turn it down with: under a small max_tokens it can burn the whole cap thinking about a one-word answer and end the turn mid-thinking, which returns stop_reason 'max_tokens' with content []. Tokens were produced and the turn worked, so failing here reports a defect in whatever the row was actually measuring (cache counters, routing) that did not happen. Same forgiveness the openai-chat branch above gives stop-sequence truncation. An empty content array with no output tokens is still a failure.
if (!hasContent && j.stop_reason === 'max_tokens' && j.usage && j.usage.output_tokens > 0) { hasContent = true; }
// Image-output models (responseModalities IMAGE) answer with inlineData parts only; the image IS the content.
hasContent = parts.some(function (p) { return p && (p.text || p.functionCall || p.executableCode || (p.inlineData && p.inlineData.data)); });

// Responses tool-use items are all typed <tool>_call (function_call, tool_search_call, custom_tool_call, mcp_call, local_shell_call, ...). A client-execution call is a valid TERMINAL output: the model emits the call and stops, waiting for the matching *_output, so no text accompanies it.
hasContent = j.embeddings.every(function (e) { return e && Array.isArray(e.values) && e.values.length > 0; });

// Nova answers with an array of {embedding, embeddingType} OBJECTS, where Bedrock Cohere answers with an array of bare vectors. Claimed before that branch, which matches on `embeddings` alone and would find no content in an array of objects - the failure that surfaced when folder 114 landed.
hasContent = j.embeddings.every(function (e) { return e && Array.isArray(e.embedding) && e.embedding.length > 0; });

} else if (Array.isArray(j.results) && j.results.length > 0 && j.results[0] && typeof j.results[0].index === 'number' && (typeof j.results[0].relevance_score === 'number' || typeof j.results[0].relevanceScore === 'number')) {

// A rerank response ranks the documents it was given; it generates no text, so the ranked list IS the content. Matched on index + a relevance score rather than on `results` alone, which is too generic to claim off other shapes. This branch went missing until now because no rerank row had ever returned 2xx: every bedrock row was rejected pre-flight for not naming its model as an ARN, and every vertex row 403s on discoveryengine IAM - and the content check is gated on code < 400, so it never ran.
} else if (Array.isArray(j.records) && j.records.length > 0 && j.records[0] && typeof j.records[0].id === 'string' && typeof j.records[0].score === 'number') {

// Discovery Engine's rank API is ID-keyed: it answers with records[] carrying id + score, not results[] with index + relevance_score, so the rerank branch above never claims it. Like that branch, the ranked list IS the content - a rank call generates no text. Matched on id + score rather than on `records` alone, which is too generic to claim off other shapes. This went missing because /genai/v1/rank only started returning the real Discovery Engine shape once the rank response converter landed; before that it leaked Bifrost's canonical results[] and was claimed by the rerank branch.
// An async video job is a receipt, not content: submit returns {id, status} and
// the rendered asset only exists after polling. The id IS the payload.
} else if (typeof j.status === 'string' && typeof j.id === 'string' && (j.request_id || j.created_at)) {
// An async job is a receipt, not content: submit returns {id, status} and the result
// only exists once the job completes. The id IS the payload.
pm.expect(hasContent, 'expected non-empty content (shape=' + shape + ', body=' + JSON.stringify(j).slice(0, 200) + ')').to.be.true;
// Routed-identity response headers (x-bifrost-*): present on every successful
// inference response, streaming and non-streaming, on native /v1 and every
// drop-in integration route, and passthrough (section 9) inference routes
// (all funnel through handleRequest, so RoutingInfo is populated).
// Management/list/file/batch/count ops are excluded by the positive path
// only when a fallback or key-alias fires) so they are not asserted here, and
// x-bifrost-routing-info-key is omitted (depends on operator key-naming).
// Streaming terminator contract for OpenAI-shaped completion streams (#7065).
// Bifrost writes a single `data: [DONE]` as the LAST frame of every successful
// /chat/completions and /completions SSE response, native and /openai drop-in,
// after any usage-only chunk (stream_options.include_usage) and after the
// post-hooks. A stream that ended on an error frame deliberately gets no marker,
// so the check stands down when a frame carries a top-level `error`.
// Responses, Anthropic, GenAI, Bedrock and image streams terminate differently
pm.test('SSE stream ends with a single [DONE] after any usage frame - #7065', function () {
pm.expect(__doneCount, 'expected exactly one [DONE] frame, got ' + __doneCount + ' across ' + __frames + ' frames').to.equal(1);
pm.expect(__afterDone, __afterDone + ' data frame(s) arrived after [DONE]; clients stop reading at the marker, so they are lost').to.equal(0);
pm.expect(__doneAt, 'usage frame at ' + __lastUsageAt + ' must precede [DONE] at ' + __doneAt).to.be.above(__lastUsageAt);

item.name: 1. Native Bifrost API
item.description: Bifrost's own OpenAI-shaped surface. Use a `provider/model` string in the `model` field to route to any configured backend.

item.name: 2. OpenAI drop-in (/openai)
item.description: Mirrors the OpenAI HTTP surface. Existing OpenAI SDKs work by pointing `base_url` at `{{baseUrl}}/openai`.

item.name: 3. Anthropic drop-in (/anthropic)
item.description: Mirrors the Anthropic Messages API. Use `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version` headers as you would against api.anthropic.com.

item.name: 4. Bedrock drop-in (/bedrock)
item.description: Mirrors AWS Bedrock's Converse API. Auth/credentials are resolved by Bifrost from its provider config (or IAM/env if Bedrock provider config is nil).

exec: // Regression: Bifrost 1.4.6 crashed with mismatch type []bedrock.BedrockGuardrailAssessment
// when trace:enabled caused Bedrock to return outputAssessments as a map keyed by guardrail ID.
pm.test('trace.guardrail.outputAssessments is a map not an array', function () {
pm.expect(Array.isArray(oa), 'outputAssessments must not be an array').to.be.false;
// Bedrock native streaming (converse-stream). Verifies the upstream is delivered
// as a live AWS event stream with multiple incremental frames, guarding against the
// server-side gzip buffering regression where all events arrive at once (issue #4542).
pm.test('Bedrock stream is an AWS event stream', function () {
pm.test('Bedrock stream contains multiple incremental events', function () {
pm.expect(body, 'expected a messageStop event terminating the stream').to.include('messageStop');
pm.test('Bedrock converse-stream closes content blocks (contentBlockStop before messageStop) - #4923', function () {
pm.expect(b2, 'expected a contentBlockStop event closing each content block').to.include('contentBlockStop');
// Bedrock streaming via the OpenAI-compatible SSE path (/v1/chat/completions).
// Confirms chunked SSE delivery with multiple incremental content deltas and a
// [DONE] terminator. Note: newman buffers the full response, so this validates
// SSE framing/chunking, not wall-clock TTFB (that is covered by the Go unit test
pm.test('Bedrock SSE: content-type is text/event-stream', function () {
pm.test('Bedrock SSE: multiple data chunks with incremental content deltas', function () {
var chunks = 0, sawDelta = false, sawDone = false;
try { var j = JSON.parse(p); var d = j.choices && j.choices[0] && j.choices[0].delta; if (d && typeof d.content === 'string' && d.content.length) { sawDelta = true; } } catch (e) {}
pm.expect(chunks, 'expected > 1 SSE data chunks, got ' + chunks).to.be.above(1);
pm.expect(sawDelta, 'expected at least one chunk with an incremental content delta').to.be.true;
// Bedrock streaming via the OpenAI-compatible SSE path (/v1/chat/completions).
// Confirms chunked SSE delivery with multiple incremental content deltas and a
// [DONE] terminator. Note: newman buffers the full response, so this validates

item.name: 8. Criss-Cross (endpoint × provider × modality matrix)
item.description:
Every Bifrost drop-in request shape × every model provider × every supported modality.

Bifrost's `ParseModelString` (core/schemas/utils.go) splits the `provider/model-name` prefix and dispatches to the right backend; per-shape converters in `transports/bifrost-http/integrations/` normalize the incoming payload to `BifrostChatRequest` (or the equivalent for embeddings/audio/images) regardless of which provider serves it.

Sub-folders:
- 8.1 Text Chat (non-streaming) — rows A-G × providers
- 8.2 Text Chat (streaming) — same matrix with stream:true / :streamGenerateContent / converse-stream
- 8.3 Embeddings — rows H-J × providers
- 8.4 Audio — transcriptions (K-L) + speech (M-N)
- 8.5 Image generation / editing — rows O-Q
- 8.6 Feature combinations — tool calling, vision, JSON/structured output, reasoning

Cells where the provider doesn't support the modality (e.g., Anthropic embeddings, Bedrock audio input — see core/providers/*/{anthropic.go:1878-1923, bedrock.go:1936-1941}) are tagged `[SKIP]` and skipped at runtime unless `include_skip=1`.

item.name: 8.1 Text Chat (non-streaming)
item.description: Minimal `Hello` text-chat request across every endpoint shape × every model provider. Native /v1/chat/completions is the diagonal (provider/model strings only); rows B-G exercise the cross-shape conversion path (e.g., /anthropic/v1/messages with model=openai/gpt-5).

item.name: 8.1.A Native /v1/chat/completions (unified, 10 per provider)
item.description: The headline demo: one endpoint, one request shape, only the `model` field varies. 5 providers x 10 models = 50 requests (Azure intentionally skipped — Azure deployments use a different URL shape, covered separately in 8.1.C and the legacy §5).

item.name: 8.1.B Native /v1/responses (Responses shape × all providers)
item.description: OpenAI Responses-API request shape (`input` instead of `messages`) against the native endpoint with model strings from all 6 providers. Bifrost's Responses-shape converter normalizes to BifrostChatRequest internally; the same converter must handle every backend.

item.name: 8.1.C OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/chat/completions × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI ChatCompletion shape via the `/openai` drop-in prefix, routed to non-OpenAI backends via `provider/` model prefix. The OpenAI diagonal is already in §2 and 8.1.A; here we exercise the drop-in's converter against backends that need shape translation.

item.name: 8.1.D OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/responses × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI Responses-API shape via `/openai` drop-in, routed to non-OpenAI backends. Responses-shape converter must round-trip through every provider's chat backend.

item.name: 8.1.E Anthropic drop-in /anthropic/v1/messages × non-Anthropic providers
item.description: Anthropic Messages-API shape (requires `max_tokens`) routed to non-Anthropic backends. Tests Bifrost's Messages→BifrostChatRequest converter against every other provider.

item.name: 8.1.F GenAI drop-in /genai/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent × non-Gemini providers
item.description: Google GenAI generateContent shape (`contents` / `parts` body, model in URL path) routed to non-Gemini backends. The provider/model prefix is part of the path; Bifrost's GenAI router (`integrations/router.go`) parses it before invoking the backend.

item.name: 8.1.G Bedrock drop-in /bedrock/model/{modelId}/converse × non-Bedrock providers
item.description: AWS Bedrock Converse API shape (`messages[].content[].text` body, model ID in the URL path) routed to non-Bedrock backends. The Converse route captures `{modelId}` as a single path segment, so a `provider/model` prefix must be URL-encoded (`%2F`) in the path — see `bedrockPreCallback` in `transports/bifrost-http/integrations/bedrock.go`.

item.name: 8.2 Text Chat (streaming)
item.description:
Streaming variants of the 8.1 matrix. OpenAI / Anthropic / Responses shapes use `stream: true` in the body; GenAI uses `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`; Bedrock uses the `/converse-stream` URL.

The folder-level test script (inherited by all items) asserts the Content-Type is a streaming type and that the body contains a recognized stream terminator (`[DONE]` for OpenAI SSE, `message_stop` / `message_delta` for Anthropic, `finishReason` for GenAI, `messageStop` for Bedrock).

item.name: 8.6 Feature combinations
item.description:
Feature-specific cross-shape tests: tool calling, vision (image input), JSON / structured output, reasoning / thinking.

Each feature is tested across multiple endpoint shapes with multiple model providers, proving Bifrost's converters preserve feature semantics across shape boundaries (e.g., OpenAI `tools` array → Anthropic `tools` shape when routed to Claude; Anthropic `tools` shape → Gemini `function_declarations` when routed to Gemini).

Response-shape assertions (`tool_calls` / `tool_use` / `functionCall`) are already in the top-level detector.

item.name: 8.6.1 Tool calling × endpoint shapes × providers
item.description: Function-calling request. Each shape uses its native tool schema (OpenAI `tools[].function`, Anthropic `tools[].input_schema`, GenAI `tools[].function_declarations`, Bedrock `toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec`). The converter must translate to the backend's native tool shape and translate the response back.

item.name: 8.6.2 Vision (image input) × endpoint shapes × providers
item.description:
Vision request with a 1×1 transparent PNG (base64 inline). Each shape uses its native image-content schema:
- OpenAI: `content: [{type:"image_url", image_url:{url:"data:image/png;base64,..."}}]`
- Anthropic: `content: [{type:"image", source:{type:"base64", media_type, data}}]`
- GenAI: `parts: [{inline_data:{mime_type, data}}]`
- Bedrock: `content: [{image:{format, source:{bytes}}}]`

item.name: 8.6.3 JSON / structured output × providers
item.description: OpenAI `response_format: {type: "json_schema", json_schema: {...}}` via native chat endpoint, routed to each provider's structured-output mechanism (Anthropic tool-use forcing, Gemini responseSchema, Bedrock tool-spec).

item.name: 8.6.4 Reasoning / thinking × providers
item.description:
Reasoning/thinking activation via the request field appropriate for the model's native provider:
- OpenAI o-series: `reasoning_effort: "low"`
- Anthropic: `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 1024}`
- Gemini 2.5+: `thinkingConfig: {thinkingBudget: 1024}` (or via Bifrost's OpenAI-shape `reasoning_effort` translation)

Bifrost's converter maps each field to the backend's native reasoning parameter.

item.name: MCP Tool Handling cross-cut
item.description: Regression #3795: a provider-side `type:"mcp"` server tool in a Responses request must be silently dropped for providers without an MCP connector (Bedrock, Vertex), not rejected. Function tools survive the strip. Function-bearing rows force the surviving function tool via tool_choice and verify it is invoked (output function_call / streamed response.function_call_arguments). Lone-mcp rows exercise the all-tools-dropped edge case: zero tools left after the strip must still return a text answer with NO tool call. Server/MCP tool calls are NOT expected for Bedrock/Vertex Claude — that is correct. Covers native + /openai drop-in + streaming.

item.name: 13. OpenRouter Prompt Caching (cache_control)
item.description: Sends OpenAI-format chat requests through the OpenRouter provider with Anthropic-style cache_control breakpoints on content blocks and tools. OpenRouter forwards cache_control to Claude/Gemini (explicit caching) and harmlessly ignores it for implicit-caching models (OpenAI/DeepSeek) — these must NOT 400. Bifrost preserves cache_control only when the provider is OpenRouter (stripped for native OpenAI).

item.name: 14. No-Prefix Integration Routes (provider inference)
item.description: Integration drop-in requests (/openai, /anthropic, /genai, /bedrock, /cohere, /langchain, /litellm, /pydanticai, /cursor) whose model carried a known Bifrost provider prefix, with that prefix removed from the body "model" field and the /models/<provider>/ URL segment. Exercises provider inference when callers omit the provider prefix. Native /v1/* and *_passthrough routes are excluded. Run with: make run-provider-harness-no-prefix-test

item.name: 8. Criss-Cross (endpoint × provider × modality matrix)
item.description:
Every Bifrost drop-in request shape × every model provider × every supported modality.

Bifrost's `ParseModelString` (core/schemas/utils.go) splits the `provider/model-name` prefix and dispatches to the right backend; per-shape converters in `transports/bifrost-http/integrations/` normalize the incoming payload to `BifrostChatRequest` (or the equivalent for embeddings/audio/images) regardless of which provider serves it.

Sub-folders:
- 8.1 Text Chat (non-streaming) — rows A-G × providers
- 8.2 Text Chat (streaming) — same matrix with stream:true / :streamGenerateContent / converse-stream
- 8.3 Embeddings — rows H-J × providers
- 8.4 Audio — transcriptions (K-L) + speech (M-N)
- 8.5 Image generation / editing — rows O-Q
- 8.6 Feature combinations — tool calling, vision, JSON/structured output, reasoning

Cells where the provider doesn't support the modality (e.g., Anthropic embeddings, Bedrock audio input — see core/providers/*/{anthropic.go:1878-1923, bedrock.go:1936-1941}) are tagged `[SKIP]` and skipped at runtime unless `include_skip=1`.

item.name: 8.1 Text Chat (non-streaming)
item.description: Minimal `Hello` text-chat request across every endpoint shape × every model provider. Native /v1/chat/completions is the diagonal (provider/model strings only); rows B-G exercise the cross-shape conversion path (e.g., /anthropic/v1/messages with model=openai/gpt-5).

item.name: 8.1.C OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/chat/completions × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI ChatCompletion shape via the `/openai` drop-in prefix, routed to non-OpenAI backends via `provider/` model prefix. The OpenAI diagonal is already in §2 and 8.1.A; here we exercise the drop-in's converter against backends that need shape translation.

item.name: 8.1.D OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/responses × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI Responses-API shape via `/openai` drop-in, routed to non-OpenAI backends. Responses-shape converter must round-trip through every provider's chat backend.

item.name: 8.1.E Anthropic drop-in /anthropic/v1/messages × non-Anthropic providers
item.description: Anthropic Messages-API shape (requires `max_tokens`) routed to non-Anthropic backends. Tests Bifrost's Messages→BifrostChatRequest converter against every other provider.

item.name: 8.1.F GenAI drop-in /genai/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent × non-Gemini providers
item.description: Google GenAI generateContent shape (`contents` / `parts` body, model in URL path) routed to non-Gemini backends. The provider/model prefix is part of the path; Bifrost's GenAI router (`integrations/router.go`) parses it before invoking the backend.

item.name: 8.2 Text Chat (streaming)
item.description:
Streaming variants of the 8.1 matrix. OpenAI / Anthropic / Responses shapes use `stream: true` in the body; GenAI uses `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`; Bedrock uses the `/converse-stream` URL.

The folder-level test script (inherited by all items) asserts the Content-Type is a streaming type and that the body contains a recognized stream terminator (`[DONE]` for OpenAI SSE, `message_stop` / `message_delta` for Anthropic, `finishReason` for GenAI, `messageStop` for Bedrock).

item.description: OpenAI streaming chat shape via drop-in, routed to non-OpenAI backends.

item.name: 8.2.D OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/responses streaming × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI streaming Responses shape via drop-in, routed to non-OpenAI backends.

item.name: 8.2.E Anthropic drop-in /anthropic/v1/messages streaming × non-Anthropic providers
item.description: Anthropic streaming Messages-API shape via drop-in, routed to non-Anthropic backends.

item.name: 8.2.F GenAI drop-in :streamGenerateContent × non-Gemini providers
item.description: Google GenAI streaming via `:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`, routed to non-Gemini backends. Body unchanged from non-streaming generateContent; SSE is requested via the URL suffix + query.

item.name: 8.3 Embeddings
item.description:
Embedding endpoints × providers. Anthropic returns NewUnsupportedOperationError for Embedding (core/providers/anthropic/anthropic.go:1878-1923) — those cells are tagged `[SKIP]` and skipped unless `include_skip=1`.

Response shapes (validated by extended top-level detector):
- OpenAI: `{data: [{embedding: [...]}]}` → list-data branch
- GenAI: `{embedding: {values: [...]}}` → genai-embedding branch
- Bedrock Titan: `{embedding: [...]}` → bedrock-titan-embedding branch
- Vertex: `{predictions: [{embeddings: {values}}]}` → vertex-predictions branch

item.name: 8.3.I OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/embeddings × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI Embeddings shape via drop-in, routed to non-OpenAI backends.

item.name: 8.3.J GenAI drop-in /genai/v1beta/models/{model}:embedContent × non-Gemini providers
item.description: Google GenAI embedContent shape (`content.parts`), model in URL path. Routed to non-Gemini embedding backends.

item.name: 8.4 Audio (transcription + speech)
item.description:
Audio endpoints × providers. Most providers don't expose a dedicated audio endpoint through Bifrost — those cells are `[SKIP]`:
- Anthropic: no audio (core/providers/anthropic/anthropic.go:1878-1923)
- Vertex: no transcription (core/providers/vertex/vertex.go:1722-1729)
- Bedrock: no transcription (core/providers/bedrock/bedrock.go:1936-1941); audio input rejected (core/providers/bedrock/utils.go:1058)
- Gemini/Vertex TTS: no /v1/audio/speech equivalent

Transcription tests require `tests/e2e/api/fixtures/sample.mp3` (small audio sample) at runtime — see Phase 7 verification.

Response shapes (validated by extended top-level detector):
- Transcription JSON: `{text: "..."}` → audio-transcription branch
- TTS binary: `audio/*` Content-Type → prelude's non-JSON early-return passes status-only check

item.name: 8.4.N OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/audio/speech × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI TTS shape via drop-in. Only Azure has a comparable backend.

item.name: 8.5 Image generation
item.description:
Image generation endpoints × providers. Anthropic returns NewUnsupportedOperationError for ImageGeneration (core/providers/anthropic/anthropic.go:1878-1923) — those cells are `[SKIP]`.

Response shapes (validated by extended top-level detector):
- OpenAI: `{data: [{url|b64_json}]}` → list-data branch
- Vertex Imagen: `{predictions: [{bytesBase64Encoded}]}` → vertex-predictions branch
- Bedrock Titan/Nova: `{images: ["base64"]}` → bedrock-images branch

Omits /v1/images/edits — needs a binary PNG fixture; will be added later if needed.

item.name: 8.5.P OpenAI drop-in /openai/v1/images/generations × non-OpenAI providers
item.description: OpenAI image-generation shape via drop-in, routed to non-OpenAI backends.

item.name: 8.6 Feature combinations
item.description:
Feature-specific cross-shape tests: tool calling, vision (image input), JSON / structured output, reasoning / thinking.

Each feature is tested across multiple endpoint shapes with multiple model providers, proving Bifrost's converters preserve feature semantics across shape boundaries (e.g., OpenAI `tools` array → Anthropic `tools` shape when routed to Claude; Anthropic `tools` shape → Gemini `function_declarations` when routed to Gemini).

Response-shape assertions (`tool_calls` / `tool_use` / `functionCall`) are already in the top-level detector.

item.name: 8.6.1 Tool calling × endpoint shapes × providers
item.description: Function-calling request. Each shape uses its native tool schema (OpenAI `tools[].function`, Anthropic `tools[].input_schema`, GenAI `tools[].function_declarations`, Bedrock `toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec`). The converter must translate to the backend's native tool shape and translate the response back.

item.name: 8.6.2 Vision (image input) × endpoint shapes × providers
item.description:
Vision request with a 1×1 transparent PNG (base64 inline). Each shape uses its native image-content schema:
- OpenAI: `content: [{type:"image_url", image_url:{url:"data:image/png;base64,..."}}]`
- Anthropic: `content: [{type:"image", source:{type:"base64", media_type, data}}]`
- GenAI: `parts: [{inline_data:{mime_type, data}}]`
- Bedrock: `content: [{image:{format, source:{bytes}}}]`

item.name: 8.6.4 Reasoning / thinking × providers
item.description:
Reasoning/thinking activation via the request field appropriate for the model's native provider:
- OpenAI o-series: `reasoning_effort: "low"`
- Anthropic: `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: 1024}`
- Gemini 2.5+: `thinkingConfig: {thinkingBudget: 1024}` (or via Bifrost's OpenAI-shape `reasoning_effort` translation)

Bifrost's converter maps each field to the backend's native reasoning parameter.

item.name: 11. Cross-Provider Feature Tests
item.description: Same feature exercised across multiple providers via Bifrost's unified routing. Each sub-folder is one capability; each request differs only by `model` (or path) to show that Bifrost translates the request shape per-provider.

item.name: 21. Responses Stream Usage Persistence (#4846 / PR #4899)
item.description: Regression coverage for PR #4899 (fixes #4846): the final response.completed SSE event of a Responses stream carries response.usage, but the streaming accumulator dedupes chunks by ChunkIndex and reads stream metadata from the highest index. OpenAI-compatible Responses streams set ChunkIndex from the provider's sequence_number (core/providers/openai/openai.go), so providers that omit or reuse sequence_number (e.g. Unsloth via Codex CLI) delivered the terminal event with an already-seen index - it was deduped away and LLM Logs persisted 0/0 tokens with no raw JSON. The fix remaps late terminal events to a reserved trailing index. These cases pin the end-to-end invariant (usage on the wire implies usage in the logs DB) via the dbverify reporter (x-request-id + x-bf-expect-cost, asserting cost>0 && total_tokens>0), across the native OpenAI Responses SSE path and the converted Anthropic path, with a non-streaming baseline to isolate streaming-specific failures. Note: live OpenAI numbers its events correctly, so the exact omitted-sequence_number trigger is pinned by the Go unit test in PR #4899; a faithful harness repro would need an OpenAI-compatible mock provider in the gateway config.

item.name: 24. Responses Structured Output Schema Key Order (#5148 / PR #5151)
item.description: Issue #5148 / PR #5151: Bifrost alphabetized every nested object inside a Responses request's text.format.schema (schema fields were map[string]any and the outbound marshal uses SortMapKeys), violating OpenAI's documented Structured Outputs key-ordering contract. Under constrained decoding, schema key order steers anyOf branch selection: alphabetizing TextPart {type, text} into {text, type} makes the natural '{"type":' opener grammatically eliminate the TextPart branch, locking generation into the sibling WebCitation branch - schema-valid but fabricated output (0/5 correct pre-fix, 5/5 direct-to-OpenAI and post-fix). PR #5151 migrates the schema-bearing fields to OrderedMap. These cases send the issue's exact discriminated-union schema (each $defs member declares its 'type' discriminator before the payload field, deliberately non-alphabetical) and assert the model returns the requested TextPart, not a fabricated cite:web citation, across the native non-streaming, native streaming, and /openai drop-in decode paths.

item.name: 25. DeepSeek Anthropic-Compatible Migration
item.description:
DeepSeek's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (/anthropic/v1/messages, x-api-key auth) is opt-in: ResolveUseAnthropicEndpoints (core/providers/anthropic/utils.go) reads the resolved alias config, then key.use_anthropic_endpoints, and falls back to the OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions wire when neither is set. The shared harness DeepSeek key deliberately leaves the flag unset so the ~240 other deepseek rows keep pinning the OpenAI-compatible path; this folder targets the deepseek-v4-flash-anthropic alias declared on that key in tests/integrations/python/config.json, which carries use_anthropic_endpoints: true (#7610).

Every row asserts the OUTBOUND payload via extra_fields.raw_request, not just the response: the Anthropic wire carries max_tokens and content-block arrays, the OpenAI-compatible wire carries max_completion_tokens and plain strings. Before #7610 the rows only asserted on the response, which is identical on both wires, so they passed for months without ever reaching /anthropic/v1/messages.

Cases: (1) chat completions non-streaming and (2) streaming (raw_request is attached to the final SSE frame), (3) two independent tools requested in one turn come back as two tool_calls, (4) native /v1/responses (no chat-completion fallback). All four cases send reasoning.effort none, which reaches the wire as thinking.type disabled (each row asserts it): DeepSeek's Anthropic endpoint thinks by default and thinking tokens count toward max_tokens, so a reasoning-on turn at a small budget returns stop_reason length with a reasoning item and no message item.

pm.expect(rr.max_tokens, 'max_tokens absent - request went out on the OpenAI-compatible wire: ' + wire).to.be.a('number');
pm.expect(rr.max_completion_tokens, 'max_completion_tokens present - request went out on the OpenAI-compatible wire: ' + wire).to.be.undefined;

item.name: 26. Anthropic Native Server-Side Fallback (fallbacks shape overload)
item.description:
Pins the overloaded request-level `fallbacks` wire key on /anthropic/v1/messages.
Two unrelated features share the key and are disambiguated by element shape:
  - array of STRINGS  ("provider/model") = Bifrost cross-provider gateway fallback.
  - array of OBJECTS  ([{"model": "..."}]) = Anthropic native server-side fallback
    (beta server-side-fallback-2026-06-01, refusal fallback).

Regressions pinned:
  1. Object-form fallbacks used to fail Bifrost-side unmarshalling with 'Invalid JSON'
     because AnthropicMessageRequest.Fallbacks was typed []string. It is now a shape
     tolerant union, so both forms parse.
  2. Native (object) fallbacks are Anthropic-only. Forwarding them to Vertex, Bedrock,
     Bedrock Mantle or Azure produced a live 400 'fallbacks: Extra inputs are not
     permitted', because AddMissingBetaHeadersToContext correctly withholds the beta
     header there while the field was still forwarded. Bifrost now strips native
     entries fail-closed for providers whose ProviderFeatures.ServerSideFallback is
     false. Note bedrock_mantle is NOT supported: it is Bedrock's native Anthropic
     surface, but feature availability still follows Amazon Bedrock.
  3. Bifrost string-form fallbacks must keep working and must never leak to a provider.

Both the Claude Code passthrough path (claude-cli User-Agent -> raw request body) and
the normalized path are covered, since the strip runs on the shared egress tail.

Not covered here: the `fallback` content block and stop_reason 'refusal'. Those only
occur when a safety classifier actually declines a request, which is non-deterministic
and inappropriate to provoke in a live sweep; they are covered by Go unit tests in
core/providers/anthropic/serversidefallback_test.go.

item.name: 28. Bedrock reasoning double-emission on additionalModelRequestFields (#5108 / PR #5109)
item.description: Regression for the #5108 follow-on fixed in PR #5109. A reasoning key (reasoning_config / thinking / Nova reasoningConfig) consumed into Params.Reasoning on Bedrock Converse ingress was ALSO forwarded verbatim via additionalModelRequestFieldPaths. The Bedrock egress then carried two copies (the re-synthesized thinking plus the passthrough reasoning_config, which Bedrock expands into thinking), and Converse rejected the collision: "The additional field thinking/type conflicts with an existing field". The fix strips the consumed reasoning key from the verbatim passthrough so exactly one reasoning field reaches Bedrock. Cases 1-3 pin the integration route (/bedrock converse) that actually reproduced the bug; case 4 is a native /v1 control (the native path has no passthrough, so it never collided) guarding the invariant from that entry point.

pm.expect(t, 'Bedrock asked to remove a duplicated thinking field: ' + t).to.not.match(/Remove thinking\//i);

item.name: 31. Gemini/Vertex mediaResolution honored, request-level and per-part (image prompt tokens)
item.description:
Regression: generationConfig.mediaResolution was silently dropped in the Gemini -> Bifrost -> Gemini
Responses conversion on the /genai generateContent path, so a Vertex/Gemini image request billed the
model-default image token count regardless of MEDIA_RESOLUTION_LOW/HIGH (e.g. ~1290 instead of ~74
prompt tokens for a 1024x1024 image). thinkingConfig survived because both conversion legs handle it;
mediaResolution was handled by neither.

Fix: round mediaResolution through ExtraParams["media_resolution"] in core/providers/gemini
(convertGenerationConfigToResponsesParameters inbound + convertParamsToGenerationConfigResponses outbound).

The only external signal is usageMetadata.promptTokenCount, so each pair sends the SAME 1024x1024 image
(folder-level prerequest sets {{mediaResImage}}) and asserts the HIGH request reports more prompt tokens
than the LOW request. If the field is dropped, both fall back to the same default => equal counts =>
the HIGH-exceeds-LOW assertion fails, independent of what the model default is. 31.1/31.2 pin the fix on
the GenAI route (needs only {{genaiKey}}); 31.3/31.4 pin the same invariant on Vertex (the reported
route) and skip cleanly if Vertex is not configured.

31.5-31.9 pin the second, separate half: Google also models media resolution per Part (Vertex AI v1 Part field 12), and the per-part value overrides generationConfig for that part. Bifrost's Part type had no such field and Part.UnmarshalJSON decodes into a closed alias, so the key was discarded at parse time -- before any of the conversion work 31.1-31.4 cover. Reported against v1.6.7: an ULTRA_HIGH image billed ~21.0k prompt tokens through /genai versus ~22.1k direct, while /genai with x-model-provider: gemini and /genai_passthrough both matched Google, because those forward raw bytes instead of converting. Per-part is Gemini 3 only, so these cases hardcode gemini-3.6-flash rather than using {{genaiModel}}/{{vertexModel}}. 31.5 sends the snake_case media_resolution spelling Google's own REST reference documents; 31.6-31.9 send camelCase. 31.7 and 31.9 are the ones that pin the override semantics: generationConfig says LOW while the part says HIGH, and the part must win.

That override shape is required rather than cosmetic on the HIGH cases. Google documents Gemini 3 image tokens as low 280 / medium 560 / high 1120 / ultra_high 2240, with the unspecified default also 1120 (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/media-resolution). Default and HIGH are therefore indistinguishable, so a bare per-part HIGH case cannot tell "HIGH honored" from "field dropped". Pinning generationConfig to LOW makes a dropped per-part field fall back to ~280 instead of ~1120, which the HIGH-exceeds-LOW assertion then catches.

item.name: 32. Gemini Google Search grounding + tool combination (PR #5576)
item.description:
PR #5576 (Gemini Google Search grounding + tool combination). Four regressions, all of which return 200 when broken, so a status assertion alone cannot pin them:

1. Grounding annotations on /v1/responses were emitted on a SEPARATE message item whose output_text was "" , while the real assistant text carried annotations: []. Segment start_index/end_index index into the real text, so the offsets pointed at a different item entirely. Annotations must now sit on the text block they annotate, and no empty-text message may be emitted.
2. Only the first entry of groundingSupports[].groundingChunkIndices was read on the Responses path, so a segment backed by several sources kept one citation. Every (support, chunk) pair now yields a url_citation.
3. Gemini rejects function declarations sent alongside googleSearch unless toolConfig.includeServerSideToolInvocations is set (Gemini 3+). Bifrost had no way to express the flag, so it silently DROPPED the caller function declarations whenever web search was present - the model could never call them. The neutral include_server_side_tool_invocations param now maps to toolConfig.includeServerSideToolInvocations, and an AUTO/unset functionCallingConfig is promoted to VALIDATED (AUTO is unsupported in that mode).
4. On the streaming genai passthrough, groundingMetadata.searchEntryPoint was lost: the rendered-content output_item.done event carried no item, so the reverse conversion never rebuilt it. Google requires rendering Search Suggestions, so its loss is a compliance issue, not cosmetic.

Cases 32.3/32.4 use gemini-3.6-flash because tool combination is Gemini 3+ only.

item.name: 33. Codex additional_tools hoist + tool_search wire shapes (Bedrock Mantle)
item.description:
Codex code-mode models (gpt-5.6-sol, tool_mode=code_mode / use_responses_lite=true) declare their tools inside the input array as an `additional_tools` developer item rather than in the top-level `tools` param. api.openai.com accepts that item natively; Bedrock Mantle's OpenAI-compatible surface (bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/openai/v1/responses) validates `input` against the standard union and rejects the whole request with 400 "invalid request body: Invalid 'input': value did not match any expected variant".

Bifrost resolves this in ToOpenAIResponsesRequest: for providers whose ResponsesFeatureSupport.AdditionalToolsItem is false (bedrock, bedrock_mantle), the item's tools are hoisted into the top-level `tools` param and the item is dropped from `input`. OpenAI keeps the item verbatim via ResponsesMessage.rawPreserved.

The nested tools are the fragile part: each entry carries its own `type` discriminator, and custom tools carry a lark `format` while namespace tools carry a nested `tools` list. A typed decode strips those, which is why the item round-trips through rawPreserved rather than a typed model.

Cases 33.1-33.3 pin the hoist (a 400 here means it stopped running). 33.4 pins that OpenAI still receives the item natively. 33.5-33.6 pin the sibling raw-preserved items: tool_search_call `arguments` must stay a JSON object (function_call uses a string) and tool_search_output `tools[].type` must survive replay.

item.name: 34. Gemini/Vertex countTokens full-prompt accounting (PR #5620)
item.description:
Regression: CountTokens unconditionally deleted systemInstruction, generationConfig and toolConfig from the
request body for BOTH Gemini and Vertex, so :countTokens reported only the "contents" token count. Reported
case: a ~7.4k-token system prompt plus a tool declaration counted as 17 tokens on Vertex.

The two endpoints need opposite request shapes, which is why one strip broke both:
  - Gemini (generativelanguage): CountTokensRequest accepts only "contents" and "generateContentRequest".
    systemInstruction/tools/toolConfig/generationConfig are 400 "Unknown name" at the top level and must be
    wrapped in the envelope. Top-level "contents"/"model" are then SILENTLY IGNORED, so the body must carry
    the envelope and nothing beside it. Before the fix, "tools" was never stripped, so any tool-bearing
    countTokens was a hard 400 rather than an undercount.
  - Vertex (aiplatform): CountTokensRequest takes contents/systemInstruction/tools/generationConfig FLAT and
    has no envelope. Only toolConfig (plus safetySettings/cachedContent/serviceTier/labels) is rejected.

The /genai ingress must therefore parse both shapes and emit whichever the resolved provider requires, and
the Bifrost-only "fallbacks" routing field must be honoured for routing yet stripped before the upstream call.

Assertions are relative, not absolute: token counts drift across model versions, so each provider records a
contents-only baseline and every later case asserts the count exceeds it. A dropped field collapses the count
back to the baseline, which is exactly what these cases catch. 400 is deliberately NOT in the infra guard —
for the tools/toolConfig/fallbacks cases a 400 IS the regression signature.

item.name: 35. Gemini/Vertex googleSearch grounding filters + retrievalConfig (/genai)
item.description:
Google Search grounding fields on the /genai route that had zero harness coverage: googleSearch.excludeDomains, googleSearch.timeRangeFilter (both camelCase and snake_case), and toolConfig.retrievalConfig.latLng on the request side, plus groundingMetadata fidelity on the response side for both non-streaming and streaming.

The /genai route is NOT passthrough: the request crosses Gemini JSON -> BifrostResponsesRequest -> Gemini JSON, and the response crosses back the same way. Every one of these fields therefore has two chances to be silently dropped, and a dropped field still returns 200 - the model just quietly runs an unfiltered search. So the assertions are on response content, not status:

- excludeDomains / timeRangeFilter / retrievalConfig.latLng have no distinctive response signature, so they are pinned by the fact that the provider accepts them AND still grounds. A mangled or misnamed field is a 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT from Google; a dropped tool means no groundingMetadata at all.
- excludeDomains is Vertex-only - the Gemini Developer API does not accept it - so every case carrying it runs on Vertex alone. timeRangeFilter and retrievalConfig.latLng run on both.
- The latLng cases additionally assert no functionCallingConfig was synthesized: Gemini rejects functionCallingConfig without function declarations, so rebuilding toolConfig for latLng must not pull one in.
- The snake_case cases pin GoogleSearch.UnmarshalJSON's alias handling: time_range_filter on Gemini, exclude_domains + time_range_filter together on Vertex.
- The fidelity cases pin what must survive the four conversions: webSearchQueries, a citable uri on every grounding chunk, searchEntryPoint.renderedContent (Google requires rendering Search Suggestions), and groundingSupports[].groundingChunkIndices that stay in-bounds and de-duplicated.

Each case runs on both providers via the provider-prefixed model form (/genai/v1beta/models/gemini/... and /genai/v1beta/models/vertex/...), so PROVIDER=gemini and PROVIDER=vertex both exercise the full set against their own backend.

Not covered here: googleSearch.searchTypes (Grounding with Google Image Search) and the imageSearchQueries / groundingChunks[].image response half. Those need an image model and are deferred - Bifrost currently also drops the generated inlineData part in streaming, because processGeminiPart matches part.ThoughtSignature before part.InlineData and consumes an image part carrying a thought signature as a signature-only reasoning item.

The chunk-index test checks in-bounds and de-duplicated indices; it cannot by itself catch a regression that keeps only the first index of a multi-source support, since one index is still valid. Folder 32 pins that fan-out on /v1/responses.

item.name: 36. Bedrock Invoke Route Cache Control + Usage Fields (#5629)
item.description: Regression for #5629. The Bedrock invoke ingress routes (POST /bedrock/model/{id}/invoke and .../invoke-with-response-stream) accept an Anthropic-native request body and convert it to a Bedrock Converse call via BedrockInvokeRequest.ToBedrockConverseRequest(). convertAnthropicTools() and parseSystemMessages() only copied known fields and silently dropped any cache_control marker on a tool or system block, so Bedrock never received a cachePoint and the full prompt prefix was rebilled as fresh input tokens on every turn with no visible signal (responses stayed correct, only usage/billing was wrong). Separately, invoke-with-response-stream's message_delta never carried input_tokens at all regardless of caching, and the non-streaming /invoke response never surfaced cache_creation_input_tokens/cache_read_input_tokens even once the ingress bug is fixed. Cases 1-2 pin the core fix across two sequential turns against the same prefix (turn 1 must create a cache entry, turn 2 must read from it instead of being rebilled in full - the exact defect reported in the issue). Case 3 pins the streaming usage-emission fix independently and cheaply (no caching required). Case 4 is a regression guard: an ordinary invoke call with no cache_control must keep behaving exactly as before the fix (usage present, no spurious cache fields).

item.name: 37. Bedrock Invoke Route Anthropic-Native Content Blocks (#5560)
item.description: Regression for #5560. The Bedrock InvokeModel route (POST /bedrock/model/{modelId}/invoke) accepts Claude's native Anthropic Messages format for the request body, but BedrockContentBlock only recognized Converse's field-name-discriminated shape (toolUse/toolResult/image.source.bytes), not Anthropic's type-discriminated shape (type:"image"/"tool_use"/"tool_result"). Unknown JSON fields are silently ignored by the JSON decoder, so every non-text content block deserialized to an all-nil BedrockContentBlock with no error, and was then silently skipped downstream - only text blocks coincidentally matched field names between the two shapes and survived. Case 1 pins the image half of the bug using the issue's own reproduction shape: a request with an image block plus a fallback instruction ('answer NOIMAGE if you cannot see any image') must not get the NOIMAGE sentinel, since a fixed ingress actually delivers the image to the model. Case 2 pins the tool_use/tool_result half: a conversation history already containing a completed tool call and its result must not cause the model to blindly re-invoke the same tool (the exact stop_reason: tool_use defect observed in the issue), because it now actually sees the prior tool_result instead of a dropped/empty turn. Case 3 pins the same image defect on the streaming ingress (POST .../invoke-with-response-stream), since both invoke routes parse the request body through the same BedrockContentBlock deserialization before diverging into streaming vs. non-streaming response generation.

item.name: 38. OpenAI Encrypted Reasoning Item ID Round-Trip via Anthropic Surface (#5186 / PR #5192)
item.description: Regression coverage for #5186 (PR #5192 addresses it upstream; this harness pins the black-box symptom, not any specific internal fix): OpenAI's Responses API cryptographically binds a reasoning item's encrypted_content to the id it was issued with. Anthropic's wire format has no id field on thinking/redacted_thinking content blocks, so when Bifrost's /anthropic/v1/messages surface converts an OpenAI reasoning item for the client it drops the real id, and when the client echoes the block back on a follow-up turn Bifrost previously minted a fresh random id while forwarding the original (still real) encrypted_content - a mismatch OpenAI rejects with "The encrypted content for item rs_... could not be verified. Reason: Encrypted content item_id did not match the target item id." All three cases force reasoning.encrypted_content via include so the repro is deterministic rather than relying on undocumented spontaneous attachment. Case 1 pins the streaming emission; case 2 pins the non-streaming baseline and captures the replay content into a collection variable; case 3 replays the redacted_thinking block on a follow-up turn, which 400s pre-fix.

item.name: 40. Bedrock Invoke Route Content-Block Cache Control (#5629)
item.description: Follow-up to the review comment on invoke.go:808 (part of #5629's fix): cache_control was handled for system messages (parseSystemMessages) and tools (convertAnthropicTools) but not for ordinary message content blocks, nor for cache_control nested inside a tool_result's own content array. applyMessageContentCacheControl/injectContentBlockCachePoints (invoke.go) now translate both cases into Bedrock Converse's positional cachePoint sibling entries, and convertSingleBedrockMessageToBifrostMessages (responses.go) was extended to propagate a nested tool_result CachePoint to the function_call_output message's CacheControl. Cases run write/read pairs against the same prefix per model — turn 1 creates a cache entry, turn 2 must read from it with cache_read_input_tokens/cached_tokens exceeding the fresh (uncached) token count, proving the cache read is HIGH, not just present. Covers plain content-block and nested-tool_result cache_control across three Anthropic-family models on Bedrock (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7), a multi-tool-call turn (two independent tool_result blocks, cache_control on only one), and a cross-provider sanity pass through Bedrock Mantle (Opus 4.8) via the unified /v1/chat/completions route — Bedrock Mantle traffic never goes through the buggy BedrockInvokeRequest.UnmarshalJSON code path (it's parsed by Anthropic's own request types, which were already correct), so these Mantle cases confirm the same capability works there too rather than pinning a regression. Cases also include the streaming variant (POST .../invoke-with-response-stream, Haiku 4.5 only) for both the plain content-block and nested-tool_result scenarios, decoding the AWS event-stream "bytes" framing to assert on message_delta.usage — request parsing (BedrockInvokeRequest.UnmarshalJSON) is identical between /invoke and /invoke-with-response-stream (Stream is set externally by the route handler, not from the JSON body), so this pins that the fix composes correctly with the streaming response path too, not just non-streaming.

item.name: 41. Cross-Provider Content-Block Cache Control & cachePoint (#5629)
item.description: Extends folder 40's Bedrock-invoke coverage of the reviewer comment on invoke.go:808 across the other places Bifrost surfaces prompt caching. Bedrock Converse-native cases (/converse, /converse-stream) prove cachePoint on a plain content block and nested inside a toolResult's own content produce real cache hits when the client speaks Converse's native wire format directly (no cache_control translation involved — Converse-shaped input was already unaffected by the invoke-route fix per folder 40's regression guard; these cases pin the downstream caching pipeline itself, live, mirroring folder 40's model/streaming/multi-tool-call coverage). Azure gets one write/read pair proving automatic (marker-free) prefix caching, since Azure OpenAI shares OpenAI's caching mechanism exactly (no content-block/tool_result distinction applies there). Vertex-hosted Claude and native Anthropic (/anthropic/v1/messages) both get the same two scenarios as folder 40 (plain content-block and nested-tool_result cache_control) using their own genuine Anthropic-dialect wire format -- Vertex-Claude's usage surfaces through the unified /v1/chat/completions route in OpenAI-shape (prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens), while native Anthropic returns its own snake_case usage fields directly. OpenAI itself is intentionally not duplicated here -- Cross-Cut Round 31 already has strong write/read prompt-caching coverage for it, and OpenAI's caching is fully automatic prefix-matching with no cache_control/cachePoint marker concept, so there's no content-block-specific angle to add. OpenAI itself is also covered here, structurally analogous to the other providers' two scenarios even though OpenAI's caching is fully automatic prefix-matching with no cache_control/cachePoint marker: one write/read pair primes/reads the cache from a large non-system content block (Round 31 and the existing 'system reuse' backlog case only exercise the system-message case), and a second pair does the same across a full tool-call turn whose tool result is the large prefix, the structural counterpart to every other provider's nested-tool_result scenario in this folder.

item.name: 42. Cohere Encrypted Reasoning Round-Trip (PR #5982)
item.description: Regression coverage for the Cohere half of PR #5982. Cohere's API has no encrypted-reasoning field, so a replay token travels out inside a thinking block marked '[ENCRYPTED_REASONING: ...]'. That was only half a round trip: egress wrote the marker, and nothing on ingress read it back, so every thinking block - marker included - was mapped to ordinary reasoning text. The token never reached ResponsesReasoning.EncryptedContent, and the marker itself leaked to clients as visible model reasoning, then got replayed as if it were content. Case 1 pins that reasoning comes back as a reasoning item and captures the turn; case 2 replays it and asserts both that the replay is accepted and that the transport marker never appears in the response.

item.name: 43. Gemini Reasoning Signature Replay (PR #5982)
item.description: Multi-turn reasoning replay for Gemini through /v1/responses. Gemini returns a thought signature on reasoning that accompanies a function call, and requires it back unmodified when the tool result is sent - a dropped or rewritten signature is rejected on the continuation, so a converter that keeps only part of a reasoning item fails here and nowhere else. The harness had 71 reasoning rows and not one that replayed reasoning back on a second turn, which is the only shape that exercises this. Case 1 captures a reasoning + function_call turn; case 2 replays it with the tool result.

item.name: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash /v1/responses reasoning + tool call captures replay input - PR #5982

exec: pm.test('Gemini returns reasoning alongside the tool call', function () {
// Asserted, not merely hoped for: the replay row skips when the capture
// stored nothing, so without this a run where Gemini did not call the
// tool passes green having tested no signature preservation at all.
pm.expect(kinds, 'no function_call came back, so the replay row would silently skip').to.include('function_call');
pm.expect(kinds, 'no reasoning item came back, so there is no thought signature to preserve').to.include('reasoning');
// Only capture when a function call came back: the replay case is about a
// reasoning item sitting next to a function_call, which is the shape whose
// thought signature has to survive. Without one there is nothing to pin, so
// the replay skips rather than false-failing.
// Every tool call has to be answered, not just the first one. Current models
// emit parallel calls, and a history that replays a call without its output is
// rejected outright - OpenAI answers "No tool output found for function call
// <id>", Anthropic and Bedrock require a tool_result per tool_use. Answering
// only calls[0] made these rows flake whenever the model parallelized.
var input = [{ type: 'message', role: 'user', content: "What time is it in Tokyo? Use the get_time tool, thinking it through first." }]
.concat(calls.map(function (c) { return { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: c.call_id, output: '{"time": "21:00 JST"}' }; }));

// carrying BOTH summary text and a signature. Bifrost now sends that
// text back as a thought part, which is what this row validates against
// the live API - the thinking guide requires thought blocks resent
// intact, but does not document constructed thought parts on input, so
// only a real call settles whether Gemini accepts them.
input[i].summary = [{ type: 'summary_text', text: 'Checking the timezone before calling the tool.' }];

item.name: 44. Encrypted Reasoning Fail-Soft (unverifiable payload degrades instead of 400)
item.description:
Bifrost's encrypted-reasoning fail-soft (core/encryptedreasoning.go) detects an upstream refusal of a replayed
reasoning payload, strips encrypted_content from the reasoning items, and retries once on the same key, so the
turn degrades to a normal answer instead of failing. This fires whenever a conversation changes model family or
credential mid-flight (a routing rule or a fallback is enough) and the client replays the earlier provider’s
reasoning verbatim.

The detector originally recognised only OpenAI’s wording (invalid_encrypted_content / "could not be verified").
Anthropic refuses with "messages.N.content.0: Invalid `data` in `redacted_thinking` block" — HTTP 400 and no error
code — which fell through and reached the client as a hard 400.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT — do not "normalise" these bodies: the reasoning item must carry NO "content" key at all.
Bifrost’s own Responses output emits "content": [], and an empty-but-present array sends
convertBifrostReasoningToAnthropicThinking down its content-blocks branch, which emits nothing and silently drops
encrypted_content. The request then succeeds without the upstream ever validating the payload — a silent false pass.

A synthetic unverifiable blob is used rather than a captured one: the upstream rejects any payload it cannot
verify identically, and this keeps each case self-contained (no capture chaining, one request each).

item.name: 45. Encrypted Reasoning Fail-Soft on Compaction (/v1/responses/compact degrades instead of 400)
item.description:
Bifrost's encrypted-reasoning fail-soft (core/encryptedreasoning.go) also has to reach /v1/responses/compact.
Codex's remote compaction replays the entire prior transcript in one request, so it is the call most likely to
carry reasoning items minted under a different key or org - exactly the payload the upstream refuses with 400
invalid_encrypted_content.

Compaction is a separate top-level request shape in Bifrost (schemas.BifrostRequest.CompactionRequest, its own Input and
RawRequestBody), not a flag on the Responses request. The strip originally keyed off ResponsesRequest alone and returned
false for compaction, so the detector matched, the retry never fired, and the raw 400 reached the client - Codex surfaced
it as "Error running remote compact task" and retried the identical body forever.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT - the two cases cover both strip outcomes and must not be collapsed: the first reasoning item keeps a
summary so the stripped item survives the retry, the second has none so the item is dropped entirely rather than sent as a

item.name: 46. Reasoning × Tool-Call Multi-Turn Interleave (criss-cross)
item.description:
Three-turn conversations that interleave reasoning with tool calls, replayed across every request shape.

Each chain runs the same conversation: turn 1 reasons and calls `get_weather`; turn 2 replays that assistant turn (thinking/reasoning block intact) plus the tool result and asks for `get_flight_time`; turn 3 replays the whole history - two assistant turns of reasoning and up to two tool results - and asks for a final answer. What is under test is that Bifrost carries reasoning blocks and their signatures back to the provider unmodified through a tool round-trip, twice. Folders 19/20/38/39/42-45 each cover a single reasoning replay; none of them interleaves tool calls across three turns.

`tool_choice` is left on auto for the Anthropic-family chains rather than forcing `get_weather`. Forced tool choice is rejected with manual extended thinking (`thinking.type: enabled`) and only supported under adaptive thinking (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-tool-workflows), and Bedrock adds its own constraints on the pairing - keeping tool_choice unset makes one conversation valid on every surface. Turn 1 asserts a tool call came back, so a model that ignores the prompt fails loudly instead of letting turns 2 and 3 skip silently.

item.name: 47. Criss-Cross Matrix Expansion (section 8 completion - feature x endpoint shape x provider)
item.description:
Completes the section 8 criss-cross matrix. Section 8 covered plain chat and streaming across endpoint shapes, but every feature beyond that (tool calling, vision, structured output, reasoning, multi-turn, system messages, forced tool_choice, PDF input) was only partially crossed, and the /openai drop-in shapes carried no feature coverage at all.

Distinct from Rounds 23-26, which are NATIVE-shape drop-ins (/openai with GPT, /anthropic with Claude, /genai with Gemini) and therefore exercise the drop-in parser rather than the translation layer. Every row here points a drop-in endpoint at a FOREIGN provider, so each one pins one (request shape -> Bifrost IR -> provider wire -> Bifrost IR -> response shape) round trip.

Every feature row carries its own test script. The collection-level test asserts only 2xx plus `content || tool_calls`, which is an OR - a row with no script passes green when the feature is silently dropped in translation and the model answers in plain text. The scripts here assert the feature-specific evidence in the response, keyed by ENDPOINT shape (not provider), because the response shape follows the drop-in: tool_calls / output[].function_call / content[].tool_use / parts[].functionCall / content[].toolUse. Streaming rows assert against the raw SSE text instead of parsed JSON.

Fixtures are chosen so assertions are deterministic: a solid red 16x16 PNG (the model must say 'red'), 17*23=391 so the multi-turn follow-up must yield 782, and a system prompt demanding the reply start with ACK.

Cells that cannot work by design are named [SKIP] with the reason inline; account- or deployment-scoped cells are named [PREVIEW]. Native-shape cells are omitted from shapes C-G because they are not criss-cross.

item.name: 48. Integration-Axis Criss-Cross (umbrella drop-ins x dialect x provider x feature)
item.description:
Folder 47 crossed endpoint shape x provider x feature under the bare prefixes (/v1, /openai, /anthropic, /genai, /bedrock). This folder adds the INTEGRATION axis.

The umbrella integrations re-mount every shape family under their own prefix - langchain.go:22-37 is CreateOpenAIRouteConfigs('/langchain') + CreateAnthropicRouteConfigs + CreateGenAIRouteConfigs + CreateBedrockRouteConfigs + CreateCohereRouteConfigs, and /litellm, /pydanticai and /cursor do the same. So /langchain/v2/chat pointed at anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 is Cohere's dialect on LangChain's prefix against Anthropic's backend: three vendors in one request.

Rounds 18-22 and 27 already exercise these prefixes, but they send bare models (gpt-4o-mini, claude-haiku-4-5, command-r-plus) with no provider prefix, so every row is native-shape - the same gap Rounds 23-26 had one level down. Every row here carries an explicit provider/model prefix.

Assertions are folder 47's, keyed by endpoint dialect. Cohere v2 chat routes return the provider's raw Cohere body for native Cohere calls and convert foreign-provider responses into Cohere v2 shape with top-level message, finish_reason, and usage fields. The Cohere-family rows assert that public API shape.

Native-dialect cells (/langchain/v1/messages -> anthropic, etc.) are omitted: they are not criss-cross and belong to Rounds 18-22. [SKIP] tags cite in-repo evidence - rerank is a real implementation in only bedrock/cohere/vertex/vllm, every other provider returns NewUnsupportedOperationError.

item.name: 49. Gemini Server-Side Tool Invocations + thoughtSignature Fidelity (PR #6071)
item.description:
PR #6071 (server-side tool call support) with PR #6065/#6066 (tool combination).

When toolConfig.includeServerSideToolInvocations is enabled, Gemini reports built-in tools it ran
itself as toolCall/toolResponse part pairs instead of the older text + groundingMetadata shape.
Before PR #6071 those parts were silently dropped: the response still returned 200 with plausible
text, so no status assertion can pin this — the parts themselves have to be inspected. The
thoughtSignature bytes riding on those parts matter independently: Gemini rejects a follow-up turn
that replays the assistant content without them.

The /genai surface reaches Gemini three different ways, which are three different code paths:
  - bare model name (gemini-3.6-flash)      -> Gemini converter path
  - vertex/ prefix (vertex/gemini-2.5-flash) -> Vertex converter path (never passes through)
  - gemini/ prefix (gemini/gemini-3.6-flash) -> raw body passthrough (explicitGemini, genai.go)
All three are covered here, streaming and non-streaming, because they share no conversion code.

Cases:
  1/2. Gemini converter, non-streaming and SSE: toolCall/toolResponse parts survive, stay id-paired,
       and keep thoughtSignature.
  3/4. Vertex converter on a PRE-Gemini-3 model (2.5), non-streaming and SSE: tool combination did
       not exist before Gemini 3, and Vertex rejects the mix outright with 400 "Multiple tools are
       supported only when they are all search tools". Bifrost must therefore still drop googleSearch
       and keep the declarations there, so a 2xx with a functionCall is the pin.
  5/6. Vertex converter on Gemini 3.6, non-streaming and SSE: the same request keeps BOTH tool kinds,
       which is what PR #6066 set out to allow. Together with 3/4 this pins the version boundary in
       both directions -- the original PR #6066 gate keyed on provider alone and 400d every 2.5 call.
       These two are [PREVIEW]-tagged: gemini-3.6-flash is not published to every Vertex project/region
       (it 404s as "Publisher model ... was not found or your project does not have access to it"), so a
       default run pins only the 3/4 direction. Run with INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1 on a project that has the
       model to close the boundary.
  7.   Gemini raw passthrough: the same parts survive the non-converting path byte-for-byte.
  8.   Multi-turn replay: the assistant turn captured in case 1 is sent back in contents. Gemini
       validates thoughtSignature server-side, so a 2xx here proves the signatures round-tripped
       intact. Skips itself if case 1 captured nothing.

item.name: 51. Raw Anthropic thinking rewrite must skip the latest assistant message (PR #6110)
item.description:
Bifrost's encrypted-reasoning fail-soft (core/encryptedreasoning.go) answers an upstream refusal of a replayed
reasoning payload by stripping the unverifiable parts and retrying once. On the raw Anthropic passthrough route
(/anthropic/v1/messages) that strip is stripRawAnthropicChatThinking, which edits the client's own bytes: it blanks
"signature" on thinking blocks and DROPS redacted_thinking blocks outright.

Anthropic forbids exactly that on one message. Per the Preserving thinking blocks rules
(https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#preserving-thinking-blocks): "Within the latest
assistant message, the sequence of consecutive thinking blocks must match what the model generated in the original
request: you can't rearrange, edit, or partially drop them. This includes redacted_thinking blocks." Violating it
returns a second 400 -- "`thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be
modified" -- so the client got a different, more confusing error than the one the retry was meant to heal, after a
wasted upstream call. Earlier turns carry no such rule ("Allowed: outside tool use, omit prior turns' thinking"),
so they are still rewritten.

Cases A and B pin that no request on this route ever earns the "cannot be modified" refusal, on the tool-result
round trip (the shape the Anthropic troubleshooting page names) and on a plain multi-turn replay. Case C is the
anti-over-skip guard: the unverifiable payload sits on an EARLIER assistant turn, so the fail-soft must still fire
and the request must succeed.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT -- do not "tidy" these bodies:
 - The protected turn must be the last message with role "assistant", which in case A is index 1, NOT the last
   array element. A fix that skips messages[len-1] instead of the last assistant message passes case B and still
   fails case A.
 - Case C needs a trailing assistant turn that carries NO thinking block, otherwise the payload under test would
   sit on the protected turn and the case would stop testing the earlier-turn path.
 - A 400 is NOT guarded away in the test scripts. After the fix, cases A and B are expected to return Anthropic's
   original "Invalid `data` in `redacted_thinking` block" refusal unretried; only the "cannot be modified"
   wording is a regression.

item.name: 52. Object-store & remote URL file sources x media type
item.description:
Pins how a URL-sourced file reaches the provider, which depends on the scheme AND the target model family - not the scheme alone.

gs:// on the Gemini family is forwarded as fileData.fileUri: it is the documented form (the v1 aiplatform discovery doc defines fileUri as "The URI of the file in Google Cloud Storage"), it resolves under the caller's own project IAM with no crawler involved, and it keeps large media out of bifrost's 25 MiB inline path - which is what makes video input viable at all. Regression guarded: gs:// used to be handed to the http fetcher and died with 'unsupported URL scheme "gs" (only http/https allowed)'.

gs:// on the Anthropic family is downloaded from Cloud Storage with the request key's Google credentials and inlined, because Claude on Google Cloud accepts base64 sources only ("Input sources (URL sources for images and documents, Files API)" is listed under Features not supported).

https stays inlined for every family. Forwarding it was measured here and Vertex rejected all six 47.10 endpoint shapes with "Cannot fetch content from the provided URL ... Status: URL_REJECTED-REJECTED_FC_TOO_MANY_PENDING" after ~59s each.

A scheme bifrost cannot download is forwarded verbatim rather than rejected here: bifrost inlines only what it can fetch, and whether a source is usable is the provider's call - an answer that stays correct as provider capabilities change. So s3:// reaches Vertex and Vertex rejects it, while on Bedrock Converse it IS resolvable and travels as the s3Location union member of DocumentSource/ImageSource. These rows assert only that the rejection comes from the provider, never from a bifrost-side scheme guard.

Media types are chosen per model: Gemini covers document/image/audio/video, Claude only document/image. Images use an image_url block, because a file block maps to an Anthropic document block whose source accepts application/pdf only.

item.name: 53. Embeddings x provider x parameter surface
item.description:
Embedding coverage before this folder was one request per provider, each sending a single string and asserting nothing beyond the collection-level status check - and that check is a no-op for embeddings, because the shape branch it lands in is Array.isArray(j.data) with hasContent = j.data.length >= 0, which is true for an empty list. A provider returning zero vectors passed.

This folder pins the request parameter surface end to end: what the caller sends at the gateway, what the provider-native field is called, and what observable property of the response proves the rename survived the trip. Bedrock gets the depth because it is the only provider carrying two incompatible embedding envelopes behind one name, chosen by substring match on the model id.

Route reachability worth knowing before adding rows here: /v1/embeddings parses exactly four body fields (model, input, encoding_format, dimensions) plus fallbacks. Every OTHER top-level key is collected as an extra param by extractExtraParams (transports/bifrost-http/handlers/inference.go) and handed to the provider converter, which maps the ones it knows (normalize, embeddingTypes, input_type, truncate, embedding_types) onto native fields; anything left over reaches the wire only when the request carries x-bf-passthrough-extra-params: true. Do NOT nest these under an "extra_params" object here - that unwrapping exists only on the integration/drop-in routes served by GenericRouter (transports/bifrost-http/integrations/router.go). On this native route the wrapper is just another unknown key, so the params inside it are ignored AND the wrapper itself is forwarded, which Bedrock rejects with "extraneous key [extra_params] is not permitted". Native Bedrock embeddings are also reachable through /bedrock/model/{id}/invoke and /langchain/model/{id}/invoke; normalized and SDK-compatible routes include /v1/embeddings, /openai/v1/embeddings, /genai/.../:embedContent and /cohere/v2/embed.

Sub-folder names avoid provider keywords on purpose. runners/filter-collection.mjs matches PROVIDER against ancestor folder names as well as the item body, so naming this folder after Bedrock would hand every openai/gemini/vertex/azure row to the bedrock partition.

item.name: 53.A Bedrock Titan envelope (amazon.titan-embed-*)
item.description:
Titan takes a single `inputText` string, so Bifrost joins array input with " \n" before sending (core/providers/bedrock/embedding.go ToBedrockTitanEmbeddingRequest). The legacy/default response has one float vector; `embeddingTypes` returns one vector per requested representation. These rows pin the Titan-shaped request body reaching AWS and every requested representation coming back.

AWS request fields (docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-parameters-titan-embed-text.html): inputText (required), dimensions (1024 default | 512 | 256), normalize (default true), embeddingTypes (camelCase, ["float"] | ["binary"] | both). Response: embedding, inputTextTokenCount, embeddingsByType.

normalize and embeddingTypes are not first-class fields on /v1/embeddings - only model, input, encoding_format and dimensions are parsed there. They reach the provider as plain TOP-LEVEL keys, which extractExtraParams collects and ToBedrockTitanEmbeddingRequest maps onto the Titan envelope; that is the door those rows use. Nesting them under "extra_params" does not work on this route (see the parent folder description).

normalize is only observable below the default width: at 1024 dimensions Titan V2 returns a vector that is already unit-length, so normalize:false is indistinguishable from normalize:true. The A4/A5 pair pins dimensions:256, where normalize:false measures L2 ~0.57 against ~1.0 for the control.

item.name: 53.B Bedrock Cohere envelope (cohere.embed-v4)
