item.name: 54. Runware Provider Coverage (text, image, image edits, video, 3D)
item.description:
Runware had zero harness coverage before this folder: no cases in the collection, no entry in PROVIDER_KEYWORDS, no provider_config env file, no provider-capabilities row, and the provider was not configured in the harness gateway config. It is also the first coverage of /v1/images/edits and /v1/videos for ANY provider.

Runware is a task-based API: a single endpoint takes an array of tasks keyed by taskType. Bifrost maps its neutral `type` parameter onto those task types (upscale, removeBackground, imageMasking, vectorize, 3dInference), nests media under an `inputs` envelope, and keeps scalars top-level. Unknown keys are rejected with unsupportedParameter on BOTH levels, so a wrong envelope is a hard 400 - which is what these rows pin.

Capabilities Runware does not implement (embeddings, text completion, image variation, batches, files, containers, rerank) are declared false in provider-capabilities.json and are covered by the shared documented-unsupported checks; they are deliberately not duplicated here.

Models are AIR ids (vendor:model@version), and Runware proxies third-party text models, so rows name vendors like anthropic/google/minimax inside the model string. filter-collection.mjs routes them exclusively to the runware partition, the same way it handles openrouter, bedrock_mantle and vertex.

Runware serves text inference at its OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint, so Bifrost reuses the OpenAI handlers unchanged; /v1/responses has no native Runware route and is muxed through chat. Models are AIR ids, not OpenAI names.

Token budgets are deliberately generous on the vision and reasoning rows: the models Runware proxies there spend the completion budget on reasoning tokens first, so a small max_tokens returns finish_reason=length with empty content rather than an answer.

item.name: 54.3 Image edits (/v1/images/edits) - task types via the neutral `type` selector
item.description:
First /v1/images/edits coverage in the harness for any provider. Runware routes five distinct taskTypes off Bifrost's neutral `type` parameter - imageInference (no type), upscale, removeBackground, imageMasking and vectorize - each with its own envelope and its own output family. Masking returns maskImage* rather than image*, so reading only image* would surface an empty response; that row asserts the asset and the detections array both survive.

Model choices are load-bearing. runware:101@1 is a plain image-to-image model, while runware:102@1 is FLUX Fill, which the provider rejects without a mask ('Model is of type Inpainting'), so the two are separate rows. The upscalers run at 4x, not 2x: the 360x360 fixture at 2x is 0.52 MP, and prunaai floors that to a target of 0 and rejects it.

Covers the two upscalers a customer was blocked on: topazlabs Wonder 3.5 and prunaai P-Image.

The route takes both encodings. Multipart is the only one that can upload the image as a file, and it carries every value as a string; JSON references the image under `images` (a bare URL string or `{url}` / `{image}`) and is the only encoding that preserves the types of provider-native extra params. The JSON rows assert on raw_request because both regressions they pin are invisible in the response body: a nested `settings` object arriving stringified, and `images` leaking back out as an extra param on top of the `inputs` envelope the converter already built.

item.name: 54.4 Video (/v1/videos, /v1/videos/edits) - nested inputs envelope
item.description:
First /v1/videos coverage in the harness for any provider. Runware's video tasks are async: submit returns a task id, callers poll GET /v1/videos/{id}.

The image-to-video row is the regression pin for PR #6270. Runware moved frame images into the nested `inputs` envelope with an `image` item key, while Bifrost was still sending a top-level `frameImages` array with an `inputImage` key. 17 of 79 frame-capable models rejected that flat form with unsupportedParameter, and a further 16 reject top-level width/height once a frame image is present, because the output inherits the reference image's dimensions. klingai:kling-video@3-standard is in BOTH groups, so this single row fails on the pre-fix build and passes on the fixed one.

Both Hunyuan 3D variants are covered because they take DIFFERENT input arities - pro reads inputs.images[] and rapid reads inputs.image - so they exercise the two branches of uses3DImageArrayInput(). Sending the wrong form is a hard unsupportedParameter, and the per-model table that decides it is hand-maintained, so one row per branch is the point.

The source-video rows pin the wire contract with an unresolvable URL rather than a real clip: the only long-lived public sample is 98s, and video upscale bills per second of source. They assert the envelope was accepted and only the value was rejected.

item.name: 55. Gemini Native Batch API (create/list/retrieve/cancel)
item.description: Bifrost wires up Gemini's native batch surface (/genai/v1beta/models/{model}:batchGenerateContent, /genai/v1beta/batches[...]) alongside the already-covered OpenAI and Anthropic batch APIs (folder 12 Round 3), but it had zero harness coverage of its own. Unlike OpenAI, Gemini batch create takes inline requests directly in the body (batch.inputConfig.requests), so no file-upload step is required - same shape as Anthropic. item.name: 56. Anthropic message_start.usage Omission on Stream Open (#5885 / PR #5907)
item.description: Regression coverage for #5885 (fixed by PR #5907, db388c35c): strict Anthropic-dialect clients - @ai-sdk/anthropic, the official Anthropic Python SDK, and Claude Code (its subagent token-accounting path dereferences message.usage unguarded) - validate the very first SSE frame and crash with "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'o.input_tokens')" if message_start.message.usage is missing. Pre-fix, Bifrost's Anthropic-dialect SSE translators omitted usage from message_start whenever real token counts were not yet known at stream-open time (the normal case: OpenAI/xAI report usage only on the terminal event of their Responses API, and Bedrock Converse reports it only on its terminal event too), because a nil *AnthropicUsage silently vanished under Go's `usage,omitempty` JSON tag instead of serializing as an all-zero placeholder. Case 1 pins the OpenAI Responses API path (responses.go, the exact route in this report - gpt-model requests to /anthropic/v1/messages are always served via OpenAI's /v1/responses and translated back by toAnthropicResponsesStreamEvents). Case 2 pins the same converter against xAI's Responses-API-compatible upstream (the "Grok" half of the report). Case 3 pins the independent Bedrock Converse invoke-with-response-stream path (bedrock/invoke.go's toAnthropicInvokeStreamBytes), the route originally reported in #5885 and the one that broke Claude Code's Bedrock-backed subagents. All three assert message_start.message.usage is present as an object with numeric input_tokens/output_tokens, not merely that the stream completes.

item.name: 56. Rerank Wire Shapes and Neutral Schema (PR #6328)
item.description:
Rerank had route x provider reachability coverage in 48.6, but nothing pinned the wire shape or the neutral schema. The old assertions accepted `j.results || j.data` and only checked for an `index` field, so a Bedrock response carrying snake_case relevance_score (which AWS SDKs deserialize as 0.0) passed, and the /genai/v1/rank cases passed only while the route leaked Bifrost's canonical shape.

This folder completes the matrix and pins behaviour:
- POST /v1/rerank across cohere, bedrock and vertex (the canonical route had zero cases)
- the three drop-in routes served by the cohere provider (no prior coverage)
- per-route wire shape: snake_case on /cohere, camelCase on /bedrock, records[] on /genai, and no canonical model/extra_fields leaking into a provider-shaped body
- neutral schema: string|object documents, structured `data` bodies, result id identity, document echo as an object, ignoreRecordDetailsInResponse, and search-unit usage

Ranking assertions require the one relevant document to rank first rather than just checking for a 200, because a provider that drops document content still answers 200 with meaningless scores.

item.name: 57. Claude Code turn normalization - assistant prefill trim + mid-conversation system inlining (#6334)
item.description:
Claude Code sends two shapes that Gemini/Vertex cannot accept verbatim, and until #6334 the Gemini egress
converter (core/providers/gemini/responses.go) normalized neither, so /anthropic/v1/messages traffic pointed at
gemini/vertex failed upstream with HTTP 400.

1. TRAILING ASSISTANT PREFILL. Claude Code routinely ends its messages array with a role:"assistant" turn for the
   model to continue. Bifrost mapped it to a Gemini role:"model" content. Gemini's Content.role is documented as
   "Must be either 'user' or 'model'" and generateContent rejects a history whose final turn is "model"
   ("Please ensure that multiturn requests ends with a user role or a function response"). Gemini exposes no
   prefill mechanism at all, so the turn is trimmed. Bedrock has done this since #3517.

2. MID-CONVERSATION SYSTEM TURN. Claude Code injects runtime state as role:"system" entries inside messages.
   Gemini has no message-level system role, so Bifrost hoisted them into systemInstruction - which renders ahead
   of every message, presenting a turn-40 reminder as though it were said at turn 0, and invalidating the cached
   prefix behind it on every injection. They are now inlined in place as user turns wrapped in
   <system-reminder>, matching convertBifrostSystemReminderToBedrockUserMessage (#4068) and the native Anthropic
   fallback inlineMidConversationSystem.

Every case asserts the OUTBOUND provider payload via x-bf-send-back-raw-request rather than merely checking that
the call did not 400. A "no 400" assertion would pass on a provider that silently tolerated the bad shape and
would tell us nothing about which normalization ran; raw_request pins the converter itself.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINTS - do not "tidy" these bodies:
 - Case B needs TWO consecutive trailing assistant turns. A fix that drops only messages[len-1] passes case A
   and still fails case B.
 - Case E needs a leading top-level `system` AND a later role:"system" entry. Without the leading one the case
   cannot distinguish "inlined correctly" from "system handling dropped entirely".
 - Case G is the anti-over-trim guard: its trailing assistant turn carries tool_use, which is unanswered history
   rather than a prefill and must survive. A trim that keys only on role:"assistant" passes A-C and breaks G.
 - A 400 is NOT guarded away in these scripts - a 400 IS the regression signature here.

item.name: 60. Bedrock Kimi reasoning signature replay fail-soft
item.description:
reasoningContent.reasoningText.signature is minted and verified by Anthropic models only. A conversation that
switches model mid-flight - a routing rule, a fallback, or a client picking a new model per turn - replays the
earlier model's signature onto whatever answers next, and a non-Anthropic Bedrock model refuses it outright:

  400 ValidationException: "This model doesn't support the reasoningContent.reasoningText.signature field.
       Remove reasoningContent.reasoningText.signature and try again."

Production path: POST /v1/chat/completions -> ChatAssistantMessage.ReasoningDetails[].Signature ->
bedrock convertMessage (core/providers/bedrock/utils.go) -> reasoningContent.reasoningText.signature on Converse.
core/encryptedreasoning.go's fail-soft is what heals it: isEncryptedReasoningRejection recognises the refusal,
stripChatUnverifiableReasoning clears every signature, and the request is retried once on the same key.

The detector originally required the upstream to say the payload was UNVERIFIABLE (invalid / could not be
verified / malformed). Bedrock's wording here says the opposite - the field is not accepted at all - so it
matched no marker, no strip ran, and the 400 reached the client. unsupportedFieldMarkers closes that.

Coverage note: folder 44 pins the same fail-soft, but only on /openai/v1/responses for Anthropic and OpenAI
models - a different carrier (encrypted_content on a reasoning item) and a different strip function
(stripResponsesEncryptedContent). This folder is the chat-shape, non-Anthropic-Bedrock half.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT - do not 'clean up' these bodies. The signature on the assistant turn IS the trigger; a case
that drops it silently stops testing anything (case 3 is the deliberate signature-free control). The signature
value is a fixture and is not expected to verify anywhere - being unverifiable is the point.

item.name: 62. Files API metadata + content routes across providers (files-routes)
item.description:
Pins the Anthropic Files API route split and the mime_type/downloadable plumbing.

Two production bugs are covered:
1. mime_type and downloadable were dropped in the Anthropic <-> canonical round trip. BifrostFile{Upload,Retrieve}Response carried no such fields, and ToAnthropicFile*Response hardcoded MimeType to "", so every file reported mime_type "" and downloadable false - including tool-generated files that Anthropic reports as downloadable true.
2. GET /anthropic/v1/files/{file_id}/content was wired to the retrieve handler (its FileRequestConverter returned FileRetrieveRequest), so it answered 200 with the metadata document instead of file bytes, and no route was registered at GET /anthropic/v1/files/{file_id} at all - that path fell through to the SPA catch-all and returned 200 text/html.

Criss-cross shape: the same file id is exercised across the native /v1, /openai and /anthropic routes, and each route is exercised against anthropic, openai, azure and gemini (provider chosen by ?provider= on the native//openai routes and by the x-model-provider header on /anthropic). Azure is the positive byte-download cell; anthropic and openai legitimately refuse the download, and those rows assert the refusal comes from the content API rather than being the old metadata document.

Rows chain on {{filesAnthropicId}} / {{filesOpenaiId}} / {{filesAzureId}} / {{filesGeminiId}} / {{filesCodeExecId}} in the URL path, so filter-collection keeps producers attached under sharding and --rerun-failed.

item.name: 63. Responses -> Chat Completions Routing (Mantle datasheet + Azure DeepSeek UA) (responses-chat-routing)
item.description:
Two independent responses->chat mechanisms landed in PR #6326, plus the datasheet provider-matching fix underneath one of them.

1. Bedrock Mantle, datasheet-driven (core/providers/bedrock/mantle.go, core/providers/bedrockmantle/bedrockmantle.go, schemas.ModelCaps.SupportsResponsesEndpoint): a Responses request for a model whose datasheet row lists supported_endpoints WITHOUT /v1/responses is served from chat completions and converted back with ToBifrostResponsesResponse(). This only works because framework/modelcatalog/datasheet/params.go now compares the raw row provider before normalizeProvider - which folds every row containing "bedrock" (including "bedrock_mantle") onto "bedrock", so a bedrock_mantle capability lookup previously matched nothing and silently fell back to the permissive default.

2. Azure DeepSeek, user-agent-driven (plugins/compat/azure.go, plugins/compat/main.go, plugins/compat/dropparams.go, core/bifrost.go): Azure splits capabilities across its two DeepSeek endpoints - /v1/responses has web search but rejects reasoning.effort, /v1/chat/completions is the reverse - so a blanket fallback is wrong. compat's PreLLMHook sets BifrostContextKeyChangeRequestType=chat_completion when the caller is a coding harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) and core performs the conversion; every other caller keeps /v1/responses. There is deliberately NO datasheet-driven fallback on Azure.

Streaming on both mechanisms sets BifrostContextKeyIsResponsesToChatCompletionFallback so the chat streaming handler re-assembles Responses events; the streaming rows fail if raw chat.completion.chunk frames reach a Responses route. The Mantle streaming rows additionally pin the openai.go break on finish_reason + usage, without which a Mantle stream (which never sends [DONE]) hangs until the idle timeout.

Model choices are load-bearing: bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-oss-safeguard-20b (supported_endpoints ["/v1/chat/completions"]) and bedrock_mantle/nvidia.nemotron-nano-3-30b (["/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/batch"]) both take the fallback, while bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol lists /v1/responses and is already covered natively by folder 33.

item.name: 64. Anthropic-on-Vertex Passthrough Usage + Stream Terminal Detection (vertex-anthropic-passthrough)
item.description:
Vertex passthrough classified every response by path only loosely, and parsed all of them with the Gemini usage parser. Anthropic on Vertex is served from the anthropic publisher via :rawPredict / :streamRawPredict and speaks Anthropic Messages shapes, so the Gemini parser found no usage: passthrough calls to Claude on Vertex logged zero tokens and zero cost. PR #6639 dispatches on the publisher segment (anthropic -> Anthropic parsers, mistralai and /endpoints/openapi/ -> OpenAI parsers, everything else -> Gemini) and teaches the stream terminal detector three new shapes: Anthropic's message_stop, Google's {"error":{code|status}} envelope, and streams with no SSE framing at all (:streamGenerateContent?alt=json sends one JSON array, so the \n\n frame loop never fired and the stream hung until the idle timeout).

Every row is [PREVIEW]-tagged (run with INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1): the Vertex passthrough URL is project-scoped, so {{vertexProject}} must be overridden from its replace-me-project default, and {{vertexLocation}} must be a region where Claude is served (global or us-east5 for most accounts).

The usage assertions are the point of the folder and are made by the dbverify reporter, not by the test scripts: each row sends x-bf-expect-cost with an x-request-id, and dbverify requires the resulting logs row to have cost>0 and total_tokens>0. The in-script assertions only establish that usage was on the wire for the parser to find.

Closes two HARNESS_COVERAGE_BACKLOG entries: Vertex :streamRawPredict endpoint for SSE streaming, and anthropic_version: "vertex-2023-10-16" in body.

item.name: 65. Anthropic Egress Terminal Events on Truncated Turns (#6081)
item.description:
Pins that a turn cut short by the output-token cap still closes the Anthropic Messages stream properly on /anthropic/v1/messages.

Bug (#6081): Bedrock ConverseStream ending with stopReason max_tokens is finalized by FinalizeBedrockStream as a response.incomplete terminal event, distinct from response.completed. The Anthropic egress converter (toAnthropicResponsesStreamEvents in core/providers/anthropic/responses.go) had a case only for response.completed, so response.incomplete fell through to `default: return nil` and the terminal frame was dropped. The stream ended after content_block_stop with a clean 200 - no message_delta carrying stop_reason, no message_stop, no error. Claude Code therefore treated a tool_use whose input_json had been truncated mid-JSON as complete, failed to parse it, and retried in a loop.

Folder 17 already pins the upstream half (Bedrock emits response.incomplete on /v1/responses, #4680); these cases pin the Anthropic egress that consumes it.

Cases: (1) plain text truncation on Bedrock Claude; (2) the reported shape, truncation mid tool_use, where the open block is a function call rather than text so the block-closing path differs; (3) the same invariant through a chat-completions provider, whose finish_reason "length" becomes response.incomplete via responsesTerminalFromChatFinishReason in core/schemas/mux.go - guarding against a fix that only works for Bedrock.

item.name: 66. Databricks Model Serving and Unity AI Gateway surfaces
item.description:
Databricks serves foundation models on two surfaces under one workspace host, and the databricks provider
picks between them per request:

  /serving-endpoints          Foundation Model APIs - pay-per-token and provisioned-throughput endpoints,
                              addressed by endpoint name (databricks-claude-sonnet-4-5). Also serves the
                              OpenAI Responses API at /serving-endpoints/responses.
  /ai-gateway/mlflow/v1       Unity AI Gateway model services, addressed by Unity Catalog name
                              (system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5, or <catalog>.<schema>.<service>).

Production path: POST /v1/chat/completions -> core/providers/databricks/inference.go -> prepareRequest ->
buildURL (databricks.go) -> openai.HandleOpenAI*Request. resolveAPIFormat is what chooses the base path:
an explicit api_format on the key wins, otherwise a dotted model name selects the AI Gateway and anything
else selects Model Serving.

Both surfaces are plain OpenAI wire format, so there are no Databricks-specific converters - which is
exactly why the routing needs pinning here. A regression in resolveAPIFormat or basePathFor does not fail
a converter unit test; it sends a valid request to the wrong base path and comes back 404 from a surface
that has never heard of the model. Cases 1 and 2 are that pair: the same workspace, the same credentials,
two model names that must land on different paths.

FIXTURE CONSTRAINT - the model names carry the routing signal. system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5 must keep its
dots (they are what selects the AI Gateway) and databricks-claude-sonnet-4-5 must stay dot-free. Renaming
either to a 'cleaner' id silently stops testing the routing rule.

item.name: 67. Bedrock Converse redacted reasoning round-trip (converse-redacted-reasoning)
item.description:
OpenAI (gpt-5.6-*) and xAI (grok-4.6) on bedrock-runtime Converse return reasoning as
reasoningContent.redactedContent - one opaque blob - while Anthropic and DeepSeek return
reasoningContent.reasoningText{text,signature}. The two are mutually exclusive and replaying the
wrong one is rejected either way: 400 on Anthropic, and on OpenAI/xAI an opaque

  500 "The system encountered an unexpected error during processing. Try your request again."

Bifrost modelled only reasoningText, so it dropped the blob on ingress, left the client holding an
empty unsigned thinking block, and re-emitted that as reasoningContent.reasoningText.text="" on the
next turn - earning the 500. Only reachable on turn 2, so every row here is a capture/replay pair.

Production path: POST /v1/chat/completions (and /v1/responses) -> bedrock provider ->
converseReasoningShape() picks the wire shape from the bedrock_reasoning_shape datasheet key,
falling back to family detection -> reasoningContent.redactedContent.

The "us." prefix on each model id is load-bearing: a bare id routes to bedrock-mantle, and only a
cross-region identifier reaches bedrock-runtime, where Converse lives. The blob is minted and
validated by the model, so it cannot be fixtured - hence capture-then-replay through a collection
variable, which runners/lib/chained-vars.mjs detects so sharding keeps each pair together.

The reasoningText half of the same invariant is already covered for Anthropic-on-Bedrock by
folder 46 and is not duplicated here.

item.name: 68. Replayed thinking must stay in its own assistant turn (PR #6854)
item.description:
Two defects in the Anthropic -> Bifrost Responses -> Bedrock Converse replay path, both
surfacing as the same client-visible 400:

  messages.N.content.M: `thinking` or `redacted_thinking` blocks in the latest assistant
  message cannot be modified. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.

Measured against Bedrock Converse with real signed blocks, that refusal fires on exactly one
mutation: an EXTRA thinking block appearing in an assistant turn that is a tool continuation.
Removing a block, reordering blocks, and fusing turns are all accepted; duplication is not.

1. Reasoning migration (core/providers/bedrock/responses.go). pendingReasoningContentBlocks
   was consumed by an assistant message or a tool-call flush and by nothing else, so reasoning
   left buffered when a user turn arrived was prepended to the NEXT assistant message. That
   happens whenever an assistant turn ends on a thinking block - adaptive thinking, a
   max_tokens truncation, or a trailing block the ingress dropped - and it shifts every later
   turn one turn forward. The three chained cases replay a turn whose last block is the
   thinking block; turn 3 is the one that 400s without the fix.

2. Encrypted-reasoning fail-soft (core/encryptedreasoning.go). When an upstream refuses a
   replayed signature the strip retries once. It used to blank the signature and keep the
   thinking prose, which is legal on OpenAI but refused by Anthropic on every turn -
   "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block" - so the retry turned a request the API would
   have accepted into one it refused. The two bogus-signature cases carry a signature no
   model minted and assert the retry heals to a 2xx instead of forwarding a second 400.

The last case covers Anthropic direct on the typed chat shape: the removal is gated on the
model family rather than the provider, and stripChatUnverifiableReasoning is a separate
code path from the Responses one, so Bedrock coverage alone would not pin it.

Folder 46 replays thinking in model order (thinking first) and folder 51 covers the raw
Anthropic passthrough; neither exercises the Bedrock typed path with a trailing thinking
block, and `Invalid `signature`` appeared nowhere in the collection before this folder.

item.name: 69. OpenRouter Claude prompt caching on Responses (#6290)
item.description:
Regression coverage for #6290: OpenRouter Claude prompt caching was still broken on the Responses API after #4203 fixed Chat Completions.

Production path: OpenRouterProvider.Responses / ResponsesStream -> openai.HandleOpenAIResponses* -> ToOpenAIResponsesRequest -> POST {OpenRouter}/v1/responses.

Before the fix, OpenAIResponsesRequestInput.MarshalJSON deleted every message- and block-level cache_control and put nothing in its place, so Claude caching never activated on this route. Unlike Chat Completions, OpenRouter does NOT expose per-block cache_control through /v1/responses; the documented equivalent is prompt_cache_breakpoint on an input_text block, which OpenRouter converts back into an Anthropic breakpoint (https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching#anthropic-claude).

Folder 13 covers the same feature on /v1/chat/completions and is Chat-only; these cases pin the Responses half.

What each case pins:
  69.1 the translation itself, asserted on the outbound body via x-bf-send-back-raw-request (deterministic, independent of whether Anthropic actually cached).
  69.2/69.3 a real cache read on the non-streaming route. A 2xx alone does not prove caching, so [read] asserts cached_tokens > 0.
  69.4/69.5 the same invariant through the streaming handler, which the issue calls out separately.
  69.6 the four-breakpoint clamp. Anthropic hard-rejects a fifth cache_control block, and OpenRouter converts every breakpoint into one, so translating without clamping would turn a silent cache miss into a 400.

The [write]/[read] pairs depend on folder order and on {{cachePrefix}} (23KB, comfortably over the 1024-token minimum for claude-sonnet-4) plus the collection-level {{pcNonce}} for per-run cache isolation.

item.name: 63. Auto-injected prompt cache breakpoints (#6180)
item.description:
Regression coverage for #6180: agentic clients send no cache markers, so providers that cache implicitly slide the cached prefix onto the newest message and bill every turn as a cache write.

These cases send NO client-side cache_control at all - the client is a stand-in for Codex, which emits none (openai/codex#37674). Injection is enabled per request with x-bf-prompt-cache-auto-inject rather than by editing provider config, so nothing here leaks into other folders in a full run. The header only works because tests/integrations/python/config.json opts the anthropic provider in with auto_inject false; a header alone can never manufacture operator opt-in.

What each case pins:
  63.1 a breakpoint IS injected, asserted on the outbound body via x-bf-send-back-raw-request. Exactly one, because overshooting the four-marker ceiling is a hard rejection upstream.
  63.2 nothing is injected when opted out. The negative case matters as much as the positive: Bifrost must not spend a cache checkpoint the operator did not ask for.
  63.3/63.4 a real cache read on the non-streaming route. A 2xx proves nothing about caching, so [read] asserts cached_tokens > 0.
  63.5/63.6 the same through the streaming handler.

The [write]/[read] pairs depend on folder order and on {{cachePrefix}} (23KB, well over the 1024-token minimum for claude-sonnet-4-6) plus the collection-level {{pcNonce}} for per-run cache isolation.

item.name: 64. Prompt cache injection configuration surface (#6180)
item.description:
Folder 63 covers the auto-inject toggle on Anthropic. This folder covers the rest of the provider Prompt Caching tab: the TTL select, the injection-points editor, and the two rules the panel states in prose but nothing asserted - markers the client sent are never modified, and models without explicit caching are left alone.

Why dedicated custom providers rather than headers: only auto_inject is overridable per request (x-bf-prompt-cache-auto-inject). TTL and injection points are config-only, and PromptCacheInjectionEnabled treats a configured point list as enabled REGARDLESS of the auto_inject flag - so putting points on the real anthropic provider would inject markers into every Anthropic request in the whole sweep. The *_pc_* providers in tests/integrations/python/config.json each carry one prompt_cache shape and are inert unless a case names them, so this folder has no blast radius on the others. Their names embed the base provider keyword so filter-collection routes them to the right partition.

Vertex, Azure and OpenRouter cannot be custom-provider bases (schemas.SupportedBaseProviders is a much shorter list than config.schema.json's base_provider_type enum), so those three instead carry an INERT prompt_cache opt-in on the real provider: auto_inject false plus a ttl, which PromptCacheInjectionEnabled treats as disabled until a request sends the header. Same shape as the anthropic opt-in folder 63 already relies on, and equally inert for every other request in the sweep.

Every case reads the OUTBOUND body via x-bf-send-back-raw-request, which requires client.allow_per_request_raw_override in that same config. A 2xx proves nothing about where a marker landed, which was the objection #6180 raised.

  64.1 the TTL select, per dialect: carried inline (Anthropic, Vertex), carried on a standalone cachePoint block (Bedrock), or dropped because the dialect cannot express it (OpenAI/Azure gpt-5.6, OpenRouter Responses). Plus the absence-means-provider-default case.
  64.2 injection-point semantics: role, index, negative index, role+index as an AND, out-of-range, the neither-role-nor-index no-op, points replacing auto-inject, the last-block rule, and the four-marker ceiling.
  64.3 the same point set through every marker-capable dialect.
  64.4 a conversation that GROWS between turns: the boundary holds and cached_tokens > 0 from turn 2, non-streaming and streaming - plus the deliberate counter-example that index -1 does not hold still.
  64.5 a client that placed its own marker, in either dialect, is left alone.
  64.6 configured-and-enabled providers whose MODEL cannot act on a marker, plus the provider with no prompt_cache block at all.
  64.7 the drop-in and Responses routes, including the system hoist.

[PREVIEW]-tagged cases need a gpt-5.6 Azure deployment and are skipped unless INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1.

item.description:
The Injection points editor. Every rule the panel states, and every rule the editor cannot state, asserted on the outbound body:
  role only matches EVERY message with that role, index only matches one, both is an AND.
  A negative index counts from the end. An out-of-range index matches nothing rather
  than clamping onto a neighbouring message, and a point with neither role nor index
  matches nothing rather than matching everything.
  Points REPLACE the default strategy - the panel says so, and 64.2.2 proves it by
  turning auto-inject on at the same time and showing the default marker is still absent.
  A point marks the LAST cacheable block of its message (cache through to its end),
  the inverse of auto-inject's first-block prefix boundary.
  At most four markers, matching the provider ceiling.

The injector is dialect-independent - it writes one neutral schemas.CacheControl - but each provider serializer renders it differently and each has its own four-marker clamp. One request per dialect with the same point set, asserting the three point-selected positions survive translation.

Only Bedrock and OpenAI appear here, and the reason is a real constraint rather than a gap in ambition: injection points are config-only, config-only means a dedicated custom provider, and schemas.SupportedBaseProviders admits just anthropic, bedrock, cohere, gemini, openai, huggingface and replicate as custom bases - a gateway boot rejects a vertex/azure/openrouter base with "unsupported base_provider_type" even though config.schema.json's enum lists all three. Those dialects are covered in 64.1 instead, where auto_inject is reachable by header. Little is lost: which BLOCK a point selects is dialect-independent injector logic, already pinned in 64.2, and how a written marker renders per dialect is what 64.1 asserts.

The reason the feature exists. An agent loop replays a growing transcript; the panel promises the cached region stays put so "turn 2 onward is a cache read".

64.4.1-64.4.3 walk a conversation that GROWS between turns (unlike folder 63's identical pair, which cannot tell a stable boundary from a lucky one) and assert both halves: the marker lands on the same text every turn, AND cached_tokens > 0 from turn 2. A 2xx proves neither.

64.4.6/64.4.7 pin the opposite, on purpose: an injection point with index -1 tracks the newest message and therefore does NOT hold still across turns. That is the documented trade-off of a negative index and the exact behaviour auto-inject exists to avoid, so it is asserted rather than left to a reader's assumption.

Uses {{cachePrefix}} (well over the 1024-token minimum for claude-sonnet-4-6) and the collection-level {{pcNonce}} for per-run cache isolation.

item.description:
Every case above enters through the route that matches its target's own dialect. These cross it: an OpenAI-shaped request routed to Anthropic or Bedrock, and an Anthropic-shaped one routed to gpt-5.6.

The invariant is where injection lives. It runs at dispatch, on the neutral request, after the inbound dialect has already been parsed away and before the outbound one is written - so the marker's SPELLING must follow the target and its POSITION must follow the neutral transcript, regardless of what the caller spoke. An implementation that keyed either off the inbound shape would pass every native-route case in this folder and fail here.

64.8.5 is the case that found a real bug: the Responses serializer gated its cache_control -> prompt_cache_breakpoint translation on bifrostReq.Provider, the key the request arrived under. A custom provider reports its own name, matched no branch, and fell to the default - where cache_control is stripped with nothing put in its place, silently returning the request to the implicit caching #6180 exists to escape. Fixed in this branch by resolving the base provider first, the way the injector and providers/utils already do.

64.8.7-64.8.9 repeat 64.8.1 on the SDK-compat hosts. They are separate transport entry points, not aliases of /openai, so they reach dispatch independently and can regress alone.

item.name: 70. Forced tool choice capability flag (PR #6903 / #6887)
item.description:
tool_choice is gated by two independent capability questions, each datasheet-backed with a
name-based fallback (schemas.ModelCaps.ToolChoiceAnySupported / SupportsForcedToolChoice):

  1. WIRE DIALECT - does the endpoint accept the string "any"? Mistral and Fireworks do;
     every other OpenAI-compatible destination rejects it with
     "Invalid value: 'any'. Supported values are: 'none', 'auto', and 'required'." (#6887).
     The Anthropic integration emits "any", so OpenAI egress must respell it "required".

  2. MODEL CAPABILITY - can the model be forced at all? Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1
     removed forced tool use: tool_choice {"type":"any"} and {"type":"tool"} return
     400 'tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.'
     Bifrost drops the forced choice so the model answers under the default "auto";
     with the tool bound it still calls it. This covers the caller's tool_choice AND the
     synthetic bf_so_* structured-output pin Bifrost adds itself on Vertex/Azure/Mantle.

Controls matter as much as the regressions here: Fable 5 and Sonnet 4.6 must keep being
forced, or the gate is over-dropping and silently weakening every other model.

item.name: 71. Responses -> Chat finish_reason derivation (#6831) (finish-reason-derivation)
item.description:
Issue #6831: when a chat request targets a model whose datasheet lists /v1/responses but not /v1/chat/completions, the compat plugin marks ChangeRequestType=ResponsesRequest, core calls provider.Responses(), and BifrostResponsesResponse.ToBifrostChatResponse() converts the reply back. That converter never set FinishReason, and BifrostResponseChoice.FinishReason carries json:"finish_reason" WITHOUT omitempty, so every non-streaming converted reply serialized an explicit "finish_reason": null - breaking any agent loop that terminates on finish_reason == 'tool_calls'. Fixed by deriving the Chat reason from the Responses terminal state (status / incomplete_details / stop_reason) in chatFinishReasonFromResponses, and routing the streaming converter through the same helper so both paths agree.

Every row asserts extra_fields.converted_request_type == 'responses' FIRST. Without that guard a row silently passes on any chat-capable model, because markForConversion is datasheet-driven and the x-bf-compat header only enables the check - it cannot force a conversion.

item.name: 72. Reasoning Summary Streaming Event Fields (reasoning-summary-fields)
item.description:
The Responses streaming reasoning_summary_* events went out without fields the OpenAI
Responses streaming spec marks required and non-nullable, and the reasoning item they
describe went out empty. Reported against Gemini on Vertex: a strict client crashed
mid-reply with "undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.text')" and the session died.

Per openai/openai-openapi, all four events require type, item_id, output_index,
summary_index and sequence_number; text.done also requires text, and part.added/done also
require part ({type: "summary_text", text}). ReasoningItem requires [id, summary, type].

What each case pins:
  1-2  the four events carry summary_index, text and part (Gemini, and Vertex, which
       reaches the same converter through HandleGeminiResponsesStream)
  3    the reasoning item carries the summary its events described, all the way into
       response.completed - previously the thought text never reached the terminal event
  4    the same summary_index fix on Anthropic
  5    Bedrock emitted a hardcoded empty text on reasoning_summary_text.done, dropping the
       whole summary; the done text must equal the deltas that preceded it
  6-7  the Bedrock reasoning item carries summary AND encrypted_content, and replays
       without a 400. These two are one test split in half: populating the summary without
       the signature that signs it sends an unsigned reasoning block, which upstream refuses
  8    Gemini 3 thought signatures survive the streaming path (they were dropped entirely,
       while the non-streaming converter kept them). Gemini 3 usually returns a
       signature-only thought part, which becomes a reasoning item carrying
       encrypted_content and no summary events - so the case accepts either route.
  9-10 the reverse /genai egress reunites a signature with its text on one part, and no
       longer drops a signature-only reasoning delta (which is how Anthropic and Bedrock
       send theirs)

item.name: 75. Anthropic attachments: base64 PDF + Files API file_id across endpoint shapes (cowork-attachments)
item.description: Cowork and API clients attach local files either inline (data URL / base64 document) or by Files API file_id. 75.01-75.04 pin base64 application/pdf through native /anthropic/v1/messages (non-stream + stream), /v1/chat/completions file.file_data and /v1/responses input_file.file_data (core/providers/anthropic/utils.go ConvertToAnthropicDocumentBlock / ConvertResponsesFileBlockToAnthropic data-URL branch). 75.05-75.09 upload fixtures/arxiv-1706.03762.pdf from disk and pin document.source.type=file, OpenAI-shape file.file_id and Responses input_file.file_id, then delete. Every inference row sends x-bf-send-back-raw-request/-response and asserts the document block that actually reached Anthropic (source type, media_type, bare base64 / file_id) plus the raw Anthropic message carrying the marker; the runner enables client_config.allow_per_request_raw_override first (set-raw-override-config.mjs). Unlike the [PREVIEW] file_id rows in folder 12 these run by default: the Files API is GA and needs no beta header (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/files). Inline fixture: fixtures/cowork-marker-inline.pdf (marker indigo-418). Upload fixture: arXiv 1706.03762 (marker is the arXiv id).

item.name: 76. OpenAI image_generation tool call decode (#7059 / PR #7060)
item.description: Regression coverage for PR #7060 (fixes #7059): OpenAI emits an image_generation_call item with `action` as a bare JSON string ("generate"), but ResponsesToolMessageActionStruct.UnmarshalJSON opened by peeking at `.type`, which cannot be read out of a JSON string. Non-streaming, that killed the whole decode with "failed to peek at type field" wrapped in "failed to unmarshal response from provider API". Streaming, the per-event decode in OpenAIProvider.ResponsesStream logs and continues, so it silently dropped the two events carrying the image (response.output_item.done and response.completed); the loop then hit EOF with no terminal event and SendStreamTruncatedError surfaced a bogus 502 "provider closed the stream before sending a completion marker". The fix probes for a bare string before the type peek, and fills in the generation settings OpenAI echoes back on the completed item (background, output_format, quality, revised_prompt, size), which ResponsesImageGenerationCall previously dropped. The native /v1/responses cases are the ones that pin the typed re-emit - the /openai drop-in returns RawResponse verbatim, so it would stay green even if the typed path were lossy. image_generation had zero coverage in this collection before this folder (HARNESS_COVERAGE_BACKLOG.md, OpenAI Responses server tools).

item.name: 77. Bedrock text-format document source (#7072 / PR #5663)
item.description: Bedrock Converse rejects a DocumentSource that carries only `text` ("must set one of the following keys: bytes, s3Location") unless the document block enables citations - `text` and `content` are the citations-oriented members. PR #5663 centralized document conversion into materializeBedrockDocument and, reading the AWS docs' "only one member" union rule, made text-format documents ship `source.text` alone, which 400s for every txt/md/csv/html document (#7072). The fix ships every document as `source.bytes`, base64-encoding literal text. These rows pin that across all three materializeBedrockDocument call sites (chat, responses, tool result) and every ingress that can reach them. Each row asserts the marker is echoed, not merely a 200: a double-encoded document returns HTTP 200 with EMPTY content, so status-only assertions cannot see this class of bug. 77.07 is the reverse guard - binary documents must keep passing base64 through untouched. bedrock_mantle is deliberately absent: it routes through the OpenAI-compat path (mantle.go -> openai.HandleOpenAIChatCompletionRequest) and never reaches this converter.

item.name: 78. Bedrock OpenAI-compatible surface (use_openai_endpoints / gpt-6 path / region prefix)
item.description:
Pins the Bedrock OpenAI-compatible routing added in df47e2173, 0eaf82d19 and 473af3607.

Mantle answers a frontier model on exactly one of its two base paths and 400s on the other, so a new closed generation that nothing names falls through to the bare "v1" path gpt-oss uses. gpt-6-astra did exactly that. The base path now comes from schemas.ResolveBedrockMantleBasePath (datasheet bedrock_mantle_base_path, family list as fallback).

The "{region}/model" form is Bifrost addressing, not part of the AWS identifier: it selects the host and signing scope and must be stripped before the wire. The Converse and native-Anthropic paths always did; the OpenAI-compatible ones handed request.Model straight to the shared handler and AWS 404d it.

Responses on bedrock-runtime can now be served from /openai/v1/responses instead of Converse, behind the key-level use_openai_endpoints opt-in. Converse has no previous_response_id, so a stateful client loses prior-turn context and any tool continuation fails. The opt-in never overrides capability: Claude and application inference profiles stay on Converse.

Cases 4 and 5 require the bedrock_openai_ep provider in tests/integrations/python/config.json (same credentials, use_openai_endpoints: true).

item.name: 79. Claude Code against Bedrock OpenAI-family models (anthropic route conversion)
item.description:
Two defects made every Claude Code session against a Bedrock OpenAI-family model fail on its first message. Both live in the Anthropic -> Responses conversion and both answer with a 400, so neither degrades quietly.

ConvertAnthropicMessagesToBifrostMessages is called with keepToolsGrouped = (provider == bedrock). The grouped converter built input messages with ResponsesOutputMessageContentTypeText plus annotations/logprobs, all output-side. item.name: 80. Anthropic-ingress replay to Bedrock Mantle Responses: input_text tags + assistant status (#7074 / PR #7075)
item.description: Regression coverage for PR #7075 (fixes #7074). Claude Code talks to Bifrost through the Anthropic Messages drop-in (/anthropic/v1/messages). item.name: 78. Bedrock Mantle chat streaming keeps the trailing usage chunk after finish_reason (#7065 / PR #7076)
item.description: Regression coverage for PR #7076 (fixes #7065). Bedrock Mantle's OpenAI-compatible chat streaming surface sends the finish_reason chunk, then, when stream_options.include_usage is set, a usage-only chunk with choices: [], then [DONE]. ProviderSendsDoneMarker answered false for bedrock and bedrock_mantle, so the shared streaming loop treated finish_reason as terminal and never read the usage chunk: streamed token counts and cost were silently dropped. The fix lists both providers as [DONE] senders. Both cases send include_usage and assert that a usage object with prompt/completion/total tokens above zero reaches the client AFTER the finish_reason chunk. The bedrock/ row pins the legacy in-provider Mantle route (an OpenAI-family model under the bedrock key still hits the Mantle host and sees the same wire order); the bedrock_mantle/ row pins the dedicated provider. Before this folder no Mantle streaming case asserted usage values.

item.name: bedrock/openai.gpt-5.6-sol /v1/chat/completions streaming with include_usage keeps the trailing usage chunk after finish_reason (legacy Mantle route) - #7065

exec: pm.test('bedrock legacy Mantle route gpt-5.6-sol: stream completes with [DONE] - #7065', function () {
var finishIndex = -1, usageIndex = -1, doneIndex = -1, usage = null, seen = 0;
if (line === 'data: [DONE]') { seen++; if (doneIndex === -1) { doneIndex = seen; } continue; }
for (var c = 0; c < choices.length; c++) { if (choices[c].finish_reason && finishIndex === -1) { finishIndex = seen; } }
if (chunk.usage && typeof chunk.usage === 'object') { usageIndex = seen; usage = chunk.usage; }
pm.test('bedrock legacy Mantle route gpt-5.6-sol: trailing usage chunk carries token counts - #7065', function () {
pm.expect(usage, 'no chunk carried a usage object; the stream loop stopped at finish_reason (pre-#7065 behavior)').to.not.equal(null);
pm.expect(usageIndex, 'usage must ride the finish_reason chunk or a later one (finish=' + finishIndex + ', usage=' + usageIndex + ')').to.be.at.least(finishIndex);
pm.expect(doneIndex, 'expected exactly one [DONE] frame after the usage chunk (usage=' + usageIndex + ', done=' + doneIndex + ')').to.be.above(usageIndex);
pm.expect(seen, '[DONE] must be the last frame; frames after it are invisible to clients (done=' + doneIndex + ', frames=' + seen + ')').to.equal(doneIndex);

item.name: 79. Responses namespace tools flattened to unique names for non-namespace wires and mapped back (#7048 / PR #7082)
item.description: Regression coverage for PR #7082 (fixes #7048). The OpenAI Responses `namespace` tool container groups function tools; only OpenAI's own wire accepts it. Bifrost used to flatten it (in the compat plugin, behind should_convert_params) by splicing each namespace's members into the top-level list unprefixed, so two namespaces that both define `js` produced two top-level tools named `js` and the upstream rejected the request with 400 "Tool names must be unique". With the flag off, core silently dropped or mangled the container instead. Core now flattens at dispatch for every wire that lacks namespace support: members become `<namespace>__<function>`, a forced tool_choice on a bare nested name is re-aliased when it is unique, and returned function_call items are mapped back to the OpenAI shape (bare `name` plus a separate `namespace`), unary and streaming. The deepseek row is the issue's provider and the raw_request assertion pins the outbound names; the anthropic rows pin the tool_choice re-alias and the response-side restore; the openai row pins that a namespace-capable wire is left alone.

item.name: 80. Codex functions namespace unwrap and reserved namespace names on Mantle (#7048 / PR #7084)
item.description: Regression coverage for PR #7084 (follows #7082 and #7039). Codex CLI >= 0.147 wraps its default function and custom tools in a namespace literally named `functions` on every request (openai/codex#37022). Bedrock Mantle reserves that name and rejects the whole request with "Invalid Value: 'tools.namespace'. User-defined namespace 'functions' collides with an existing tool namespace." Core now unwraps that namespace to top-level tools, unprefixed, for every provider before dispatch: Codex treats the bare name and the explicit `functions` namespace as the same tool, so nothing needs mapping back, and on flattening wires the members must not acquire a `functions__` prefix. The same PR moved the reserved-namespace list (`web`, `image_gen`, `browser`, `python` on bedrock and bedrock_mantle) behind the datasheet row `reserved_tool_namespaces`, with the hardcoded list as fallback; the web row pins that fallback still drops Codex's client-side `web` namespace on Mantle and substitutes the hosted web_search tool, which folder 33 never exercised. The bedrock/ row pins the legacy in-provider Mantle route.

item.name: 82. Flattened namespace tool names honour each wire tool-name limit (namespace-alias-length)
item.description: Companion to folder 79 (#7048). Flattening a Responses `namespace` tool renames each nested function to `<namespace>__<function>`. Each wire caps tool names by its own documented contract: OpenAI-compatible wires, Bedrock Converse and Fireworks at 64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; Anthropic at 128; Gemini and Vertex at 128 with '.' and ':' also allowed; providers that document no limit take the OpenAI-compatible 64. The alias is now capped per base provider (datasheet row tool_name_max_length overrides), deterministically: plain when it fits, otherwise an 8-hex hash prefix plus the function name. Both rows send the same 64-char namespace with two functions (a 98-char plain alias) and pin the outbound names through raw_request: on Anthropic the alias stays plain under 128; on DeepSeek, an Anthropic-wire provider with no documented limit, it takes the hashed form under 64. item.description: Regression for #6825: a compact_20260112 edit on a bedrock/<claude> model was accepted, the compact-2026-01-12 header forwarded, and nothing compacted, because the Bedrock provider sent every Claude request through the Converse API, which AWS documents as unable to run compaction ("Compaction is currently not supported by the Converse API, however it is supported with InvokeModel", https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-compaction.html). Bifrost now routes such requests to InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream with the native Anthropic Messages body. These cases stay under the 50k-token compaction trigger (cheap) and pin the egress through the response shape: usage.iterations is only ever returned by the native Anthropic body, never by Converse, and the streaming case asserts it inside the message_delta frame. item.name: 86. DeepSeek max_tokens cap dropped on OpenAI-compatible wire (#5606) (deepseek-max-tokens-cap)
item.description: Issue #5606: Bifrost collapses an inbound max_tokens into ChatParameters.MaxCompletionTokens at the transport, then the OpenAI egress converter emits it as max_completion_tokens. DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions reads only the legacy max_tokens spelling and ignores unknown fields silently, so the output cap was dropped with no error at any layer - reported at 266-289x the requested cap (4629 tokens returned for max_tokens:16) with finish_reason 'stop'. The fix renames the field back to max_tokens in the DeepSeek case of ToOpenAIChatRequest, alongside the existing OpenCode/Ollama/Mistral cases. These rows pin the cap as observable behaviour rather than as a wire-field name: a honored cap truncates an essay prompt at 16 tokens and reports finish_reason 'length'. Pre-fix all three fail with finish_reason 'stop' and thousands of completion tokens. max_tokens is exactly 16 so Bifrost's MinMaxCompletionTokens clamp is a no-op and cannot mask the result. Content is deliberately not asserted: DeepSeek thinks by default, so a 16-token cap can legitimately truncate inside reasoning and leave content empty.

item.name: 87. Anthropic ingress non-streaming truncation reports stop_reason max_tokens (#6782)
item.description:
Pins that a non-streaming turn cut short by the output-token cap reports stop_reason max_tokens on /anthropic/v1/messages, not end_turn.

Bug (#6782): OpenAI-shaped Responses providers (Azure /openai/v1/responses, OpenAI, and every chat-completions provider whose finish_reason "length" becomes status incomplete via responsesStatusFromChatFinishReason in core/schemas/mux.go) never send stop_reason; the truncation lives only in incomplete_details.reason. ToAnthropicResponsesResponse in core/providers/anthropic/responses.go read only StopReason and defaulted to end_turn, so a 4096-token truncated reply on Azure Fireworks Foundry models was reported as a clean finish. Folder 65 pins the streaming twin (#6081, fixed in #6805); this folder pins the non-streaming encoder.

The Azure half of #6782 (Fireworks Foundry deployments routed to /openai/v1/chat/completions when their datasheet row lists no /v1/responses endpoint) cannot be pinned here: the harness Azure account has no Fireworks deployment and the gate depends on datasheet rows shipped separately. It is covered by TestAzureResponsesHonoursDatasheetSupportedEndpoints in core/providers/azure/azure_test.go.

item.name: 88. Bedrock Converse images inside tool results for OpenAI and xAI models (converse-tool-result-images)
item.description:
AWS Converse rejects an image inside a toolResult for the OpenAI and xAI families (gpt-5.6, gpt-6-astra, grok-4.6) with 400 "This model doesn't support the image field for user messages", although the same image is accepted at the top level of a user message and gpt-5.6 reads it nested on the Responses API. Screenshot and browser tools return exactly that shape, so each such agent turn failed.

hoistToolResultImages runs in both Converse converters (chat and Responses). It moves each image out of its toolResult to follow the last toolResult in the same user message, keeping result order, and leaves the fixed text "Image attached below." in a toolResult it emptied, because an empty toolResult is its own 400. It is gated on supports_converse_tool_result_images, falling back to the OpenAI and xAI families; Claude, Nova and Llama 4 keep the nested shape (Llama 4 rejects the moved layout).

Cases pin: the Claude Code shape on the Anthropic route (placeholder text, and the model actually reading the moved image), parallel results on chat completions (all toolResults first, images in result order), the Responses converter, streaming, the xAI fallback branch, and a Claude control that must stay nested. All use the plain bedrock provider, so every request goes to Converse.

item.name: 89. GenAI generateContent image requests: inline image at any part position + imageConfig aspectRatio passthrough (genai-image-generate-content)
item.description:
Two silent-success defects on native Gemini image requests sent through the /genai route to Vertex. Both returned HTTP 200 with a well-formed image that ignored part of the request.

1. Image edit detection only inspected contents[0].parts[0]. With responseModalities IMAGE and the prompt text before the inlineData image, isImageEditRequest returned false, the request was classified as image generation, and ToBifrostImageGenerationRequest kept only the first text part. The image never reached Vertex (0 IMAGE prompt tokens) and the model invented a picture from the prompt alone. Google accepts inlineData at any position; its own Gemini API REST edit sample is text-first.

2. imageConfig.aspectRatio was folded into a WxH size string by convertImagenFormatToSize, which only knows 1:1, 3:4, 4:3, 9:16 and 16:9 and defaults to square. ToGeminiImageGenerationRequest / ToGeminiImageEditRequest then derived 1:1 back from that size, so 3:2, 2:3, 21:9 and every other Gemini ratio was forwarded as 1:1. The fix copies aspectRatio into the typed aspect_ratio param, which both outbound converters now prefer over the size-derived ratio.

Cases: (A) text-first [text, inlineData] asserts IMAGE prompt tokens > 0; (B) text-to-image with aspectRatio 3:2 at 2K asserts the returned image decodes to a ~3:2 width/height; (C) image-first edit with a square input and aspectRatio 3:2 asserts the same on the edit path. B and C skip when the model answers without an image. There is no streaming variant: Vertex ImageGenerationStream is unsupported.

item.name: 91. Streaming raw_response retains every provider SSE frame (#7144) (raw-stream-frames)
item.description:
Issue #7144: with send_back_raw_response enabled, the OpenAI-compatible chat streaming
loop attached ExtraFields.RawResponse only inside the branch that forwards chunks
carrying content/reasoning/audio/tool calls. Role-only, finish-only and usage-only
frames are documented parts of an OpenAI stream, but none of them reaches that branch,
so their bytes were discarded before framework/streaming could reconstruct
raw_response - which it does purely by concatenating chunk.RawResponse. The usage-only
frame is the provider's authoritative token count and is what Bifrost bills from, so
the captured audit trail could not be reconciled against a provider invoice.

The mirror defect lived on the Responses-over-Chat fallback, where one upstream chat
frame spreads into several Responses events and each was stamped with the same payload,
making a single frame appear N times.

91.1 pins the usage-only frame surviving on the direct chat path, and that Bifrost still
reports normalized usage (proving the frame is read, not merely recorded).
91.2 pins the finish-only frame surviving, captured exactly once.
91.3 pins the fallback path no longer duplicating frames.

The refusal/annotation forwarding fix from the same change is not pinned here: a live
model cannot be reliably made to emit delta.refusal, so it is covered by the Go tests
TestChatStreamForwardsRefusalOnlyDelta / TestChatStreamForwardsAnnotationOnlyDelta.

item.name: 92. Custom provider does_not_send_done_marker keeps trailing usage with wait_for_usage (#7143) (done-marker-usage)
item.description:
Issue #7143: custom_provider_config.does_not_send_done_marker ended the OpenAI-compatible
read loop the instant a non-empty finish_reason arrived. OpenAI sends the usage-only frame
AFTER that frame and before [DONE] (see folder 91), so the loop never read it and the
synthesized terminal chunk carried a zero-valued usage object - logging, pricing,
virtual-key usage, budgets and cost attribution all recorded the request at zero tokens
and zero cost.

No fixture upstream is needed: the flag is a declaration about the upstream, not a
description of it, so pointing a custom provider carrying the flag at real OpenAI
reproduces the loss exactly. openai_dnsdm and openai_dnsdm_wait are registered in
tests/integrations/python/config.json for these three items.

92.1 is the regression guard. 92.2 pins the documented default so it cannot change
silently for operators who did not opt in. 92.3 is the unconfigured control that makes
92.2 read as a deliberate difference rather than a broken fixture.

item.name: 93. Provider error messages survive the borrowed Bedrock handlers (bedrock-error-message)
item.description: bedrock-runtime reports failures on its native APIs (Converse and InvokeModel) in AWS's own flat shape, {"message":"...","__type":"..."}, not in the error envelope the Anthropic and OpenAI wire formats use. That matters on the InvokeModel path, taken when a tool carries defer_loading, or for tool_search / context_management on Anthropic-family models (see folder 71): the request and response bodies are served by anthropic.HandleAnthropicResponsesStream, whose ParseAnthropicError reads only the nested {"type":"error","error":{...}} envelope, so error.message came back empty and the logs UI rendered no error at all while the reason survived only in the raw response. HandleProviderAPIError now seeds the message from a root-level "message" before the caller's own parser runs, and these cases pin that the reason the provider gave is the reason the caller is told. Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible surfaces (bedrock_openai_ep and Bedrock Mantle) are deliberately not covered here: they answer in the OpenAI envelope, which ParseOpenAIError already reads, so a case there cannot demonstrate the regression. The trigger is an out-of-range temperature, which AWS rejects with a ValidationException; each row is tagged [EXPECT-4XX] so the collection-level status test asserts the upstream rejection instead of requiring a 200, and if that temperature ever stops being rejected, that tag is what fails. The assertions compare against extra_fields.raw_response rather than AWS wording, so they survive a change in the text.

97. OpenRouter non-Claude models reject prompt_cache_breakpoint (PR #6692 regression)
item.description:
Regression coverage for the PR #6692 follow-up (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/pull/6692#issuecomment-5711483907): Claude Code + OpenRouter + GPT models broke in v2.1.0.

Production path: /anthropic/v1/messages -> Bifrost Responses request -> OpenRouterProvider.Responses -> ToOpenAIResponsesRequest -> POST {OpenRouter}/v1/responses.

responsesUsesPromptCacheBreakpoints returned true for every OpenRouter model, so every cache_control marker became prompt_cache_breakpoint. OpenRouter converts that back into an Anthropic breakpoint for Claude (folder 69), but forwards it verbatim to OpenAI/Azure for GPT models, and pre-5.6 GPT upstreams reject it: 400 "prompt_cache_breakpoint is not supported on this model". Claude Code sends cache_control on nearly every request, so the route was unusable.

The gate is now the datasheet flag supports_prompt_cache_breakpoints, falling back to Claude or gpt-5.6 on OpenRouter when the row is silent.

What each case pins:
  97.1 the Claude Code route (/anthropic/v1/messages) with gpt-5.4: 2xx and no breakpoint on the wire.
  97.2 the native /v1/responses route with gpt-5.4: same invariant, independent of the Anthropic integration.
  97.3 the streaming handler with gpt-5.4: no upstream rejection in the SSE stream.
  97.4 control: gpt-5.6 on OpenRouter still receives breakpoints (the field is supported there), so the gate is not over-dropping.
  97.5/97.6 gpt-6-astra on /v1/responses and the Claude Code route. The name-based fallback does not match gpt-6, so the breakpoint only appears if the datasheet row sets supports_prompt_cache_breakpoints: true; a missing row degrades to a silent 2xx cache miss, which these cases catch.

item.name: 101. Typed resource IDs stay on their upstream endpoint (PR #7307) (resource-id-path-escape)
item.description:
Pins the fix for the customer report 'Typed resource IDs can escape their intended upstream path' (PR #7307). Before the fix a caller-supplied file/batch/response/container/video id or cached-content name was concatenated into the provider URL; the fasthttp client percent-decodes and then collapses dot segments, so an id like %2e%2e%2fmodels%3f%23 on GET /v1/files/{id}/content reached GET /v1/models with the provider key attached, url.PathEscape-only call sites included, and a Vertex batch name could put a caller-chosen value in the hostname. Providers now validate every id as one opaque path segment (EscapeResourceID) with structured parsers for Gemini collection names, Vertex resource names and Bedrock job ARNs.

Three groups, all free to run (nothing is created): (1) [EXPECT-400] attack ids on every route family must be rejected by Bifrost with 'invalid <field>: ...' and never dispatched, so a 403/404/500 here fails loudly; (2) list -> retrieve chains prove the ids Bifrost itself emits still round-trip when percent-encoded in the path: Gemini files/ and batches/ names, Vertex full resource names in project-number form, Bedrock job ARNs, and the dash/base64 forms on the /openai drop-in; an empty list leaves the variable unset and the chained-var guard skips the consumer; (3) [EXPECT-4XX] well-formed but missing ids must pass the gate and come back as a provider 403/404, which pins the slash-bearing Gemini/Vertex video operation names and the percent-encoded ':provider' video suffix.

item.name: 102. Bedrock s3:// bucket cannot choose the request host (PR #7307 follow-up) (s3-bucket-host-injection)
item.description: Bedrock builds S3 URLs as https://{bucket}.{s3host}/{key}, and the bucket came straight from a caller-supplied s3:// file ID (FileRetrieve/FileDelete/FileContent) or the s3_bucket extra param (FileUpload/FileList) with no validation. A '#' truncates the authority, so s3://127.0.0.1:PORT#/x made the gateway open a SigV4-signed TLS connection to a caller-chosen host - confirmed live with a local listener. validateS3Bucket now pins the bucket to the DNS-compatible S3 charset before it reaches a hostname. These cases pin: every rejected shape returns a Bifrost 400 carrying 'invalid s3 bucket name' on both caller entry points, and legitimate s3:// file IDs plus a valid-bucket/missing-object probe still reach AWS so the gate cannot over-block. The attack cases deliberately do not skip on 500 because the pre-fix failure surfaced as a 500.

item.name: 103. Stream chunks carry only delta - no message object or empty reasoning noise (#7294) (stream-chunk-shape)
item.description: Issue #7294: with a DeepSeek-shaped OpenAI-compatible upstream (ModelScope), every streamed /v1/chat/completions chunk carried a full `message` object next to `delta` plus empty reasoning, reasoning_content, and reasoning_details fields on content-phase chunks. Bifrost passed the message object through (BifrostResponseChoice decodes both embedded shapes) and amplified the empty reasoning noise (UnmarshalJSON folded "" into a non-nil Reasoning, synthesized an empty details entry, and MarshalJSON re-emitted both spellings). Reasoning-aware clients rendered a fresh "[Thinking 0.0s]" block between every piece of the answer. Fixed by normalizing empty reasoning to absent in the schema unmarshalers and dropping the non-stream choice shape whenever a delta is present in the OpenAI-family stream loop. 103.1 pins the chunk shape on the plain OpenAI path; 103.2 pins it on a reasoning-emitting model and additionally asserts real (non-empty) reasoning deltas still stream, guarding against over-pruning.

item.name: 104. Web Search API Source Round-Trip (#7356)
item.description: OpenAI Responses web search can return specialized API sources in web_search_call.action.sources ({"type":"api","name":"oai-weather"}) that carry a name and no URL; the published OpenAPI schema does not model them yet (openai/openai-openapi#573). Bifrost's typed source schema had no name field and a required url, so a decode/re-encode round-trip dropped name and fabricated an empty url, and the OpenAI request-side source sanitization rebuilt sources without name. The case pins the client-visible path: replaying a completed web_search_call in input through POST /v1/responses must be accepted with the api source intact. Red/green note: pre-fix the replayed api source reached OpenAI as {"type":"api","url":""}; whether OpenAI rejects that shape depends on server-side validation this case cannot control, so the primary pin is post-fix acceptance of the corrected shape.

item.name: 115. Session affinity keeps a Vertex key pin with Vertex when the session stays on Anthropic (session-pin)
item.description:
A routing rule can pin a provider key on its target (the production rule was 'Claude Models -> Vertex' with key btaiops-prod-project-global and an Anthropic fallback on the incoming model). Core committed that pin to the request-wide api-key-id, and only then did session affinity run: a session last served by Anthropic moved Anthropic to the front of the chain, so the Anthropic attempt looked the Vertex key up among Anthropic's keys and died with 'no supported key found with id ... for provider: anthropic' before Anthropic was ever called. The Vertex fallback then served unpinned when it could, and when it could not the caller got that key error as a 400. Fixed in core/sessionaffinity.go: a pin belongs to the route it was decided for, so resolveSessionRoute carries pins through the session's reorder. The demoted Vertex entry keeps the rule's pin as its fallback key, which the fallback loop re-applies when Vertex is tried, and the promoted Anthropic attempt selects a key normally (or brings its own pin when the rule gave its fallback one). The trail records the move. Only requests that carry a session id take part, which is why Edge, Claude Code and Codex traffic saw it and plain API callers did not.

These cases rely on two rules in tests/integrations/python/config.json (governance.routing_rules) scoped to the harness-only header x-harness-session-pin, so they match nothing else in the suite. Each pair shares one fresh x-bf-session-id: the bind request is routed to Anthropic by the first rule, which binds the session there; the pinned request then matches the second rule (Vertex target with provider_key_name 'Vertex Global (Claude)', fallback anthropic/), affinity moves Anthropic first, and the case asserts Anthropic served. Before the fix the answer came from vertex (fallback rescue) or was the key error itself; after it, anthropic. Pinned on /v1/chat/completions and on /v1/responses, the route the report came in on.

item.name: 116. Session affinity matrix on Vertex and Anthropic (session-affinity)
item.description:
Wire-level pins for session affinity across every lever that can change where a session lands: what makes a request take part (x-bf-session-id, the Claude Code and Codex session headers, x-bf-session-affinity: off, a provider-prefixed model), what builds the chain the session reorders (routing rules with targets, pins and fallbacks, a real upstream failure that moves the session to a fallback, a one-provider chain that drops a binding), what pins outrank the session's key binding (a rule's pin changed mid-session), and what governance takes away (a virtual key whose key_ids no longer include the bound key). Every sequence uses one fresh session id and asserts extra_fields.provider, routing_info.key and routing_info.is_fallback.

Static rules live in tests/integrations/python/config.json (governance.routing_rules) behind the harness-only header x-harness-session-pin: bind, vertex, rebind, rescue, vertex-only, anthropic-first, anthropic-first-other-model and vertex-badkey. Two of them pin keys that cannot serve the model on purpose: the rescue rule's Anthropic fallback (so the promoted Anthropic attempt fails on the same model, which exact route matching requires) and the vertex-badkey rule (so a request fails at key selection without leaving the bound route). Case 12 pins that a binding names provider and model together, and case 13 that a binding followed into a failure is forgotten. The last three cases are single rows that do their own management work through pm.sendRequest: the pre-request script creates a second Anthropic key from the same env credential, a run-scoped routing rule keyed by x-harness-session-run, and for case 11 a virtual key; the test script makes the follow-up inference call with the same session id and deletes everything it created. One row per case is deliberate: the recipe forks a newman process per provider and per modality class and sub-shards a class by row position, and collection variables never cross a process, so state set up in one row cannot be consumed in another. Leftovers of an aborted run carry their run timestamp in their names and are swept by the next run once they are ten minutes old; younger objects belong to a shard that may still be running. The whole folder is attributed to the Vertex fork.

item.name: 112. OAuth2 Client-Controlled Field Lengths (RFC 6749 state/scope, RFC 7591 client_name/scope)
item.description: Regression for a customer report: GET /oauth2/authorize rejected any state parameter longer than 512 characters with error=server_error ("failed to create authorization request"), because oauth2_authorize_requests.state was varchar(512). Postgres enforces that bound (SQLite does not), so a Gemini Enterprise connector sending a 620-char base64 JSON state could never complete per-user authorisation. The same class applied to every other client-controlled column on the OAuth2 AS tables: oauth2_clients.client_name and .scope (RFC 7591 section 2 bounds neither) and the scope columns on oauth2_authorize_requests and oauth2_refresh_tokens (RFC 6749 section 3.3), all varchar(255). All five are now text; the request header block (server.read_buffer_size) is the effective limit. Case 1 registers a public client via DCR with a 1024-char client_name and a 200-token scope, asserts both are echoed, and chains its client_id. Case 2 sends a 620-char state (the reported size) with scope omitted, so the long registered scope is what gets stored. Case 3 sends a 4096-char state plus the full long scope explicitly. Both pin that the authorize step reaches consent (302 to /oauth/consent?flow=) with no error= in the redirect; redirect following is disabled on those items so the 302 itself is asserted. No provider spend. Note: against the default SQLite-backed harness profile these cases are green both before and after the fix; the bounds only ever fired on Postgres. They pin the contract for Postgres-backed profiles and against any future explicit length validation on these fields.

item.name: 114. Raw Path Authorization (PR #5765)
item.description: Opt-in auth-profile regression for GHSA-m82j-pr23-9hph and the analogous scoped-temp-token bypass. Run with provider_config/path-auth/config.json on an isolated fresh instance, INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1, PARALLEL=0 and FEATURE=raw-path-auth. The openai keyword is only a harness filter label; no provider calls are made. Cookies, inherited auth, and redirect following are disabled. Requires dashboard auth and mcp_enable_temp_token_auth. Whitelist probes use read-only GETs or invalid JSON, so a vulnerable handler cannot create provider/plugin configuration. Public OAuth registration/authorization creates only disposable client and consent-flow rows in the isolated test database. The successful consent GET proves the token is valid before testing scope escape. Every unexpected status fails. Run the whole folder in order, not individual rows.

item.name: 128. OpenAI Fast service tier bills at Fast rates and is echoed to the client (fast-service-tier)
item.description:
OpenAI renamed Priority processing to Fast mode on 2026-07-30 (service_tier "fast"; "priority" still accepted) and bills it at 2x Standard.
The datasheet stores those rates under the _priority columns. Before the fix, tierFromResponse only matched priority/flex/ultrafast, so a
served "fast" response billed at Standard (a customer gpt-6-astra call logged $0.00886 instead of $0.01772), and
BifrostResponsesResponse.WithDefaults rewrote the unknown tier to "auto" on /v1/responses.

128.1/128.2 pin /v1/responses (non-streaming and streaming): the echoed service_tier is fast (or default when OpenAI downgraded, which OpenAI also bills at Standard), never auto.
128.3 pins /v1/chat/completions. All three send x-bf-expect-cost so the dbverify reporter recomputes the logged cost from the datasheet at the
served tier (fast -> _priority columns) and fails on a Standard-rate charge. x-bf-send-back-raw-request proves service_tier fast left for OpenAI unchanged.
Prompts are tiny and uncached so Fast cost is exactly 2x Standard for the row tokens.

item.name: 115. OpenAI GPT-6 compatibility stack (Astra / Sol / Luna)
item.description:
Live regression coverage for the GPT-6 compatibility stack.

115.1/115.2 pin Astra's always-reasoning fallback on both OpenAI request converters: caller effort none becomes low, and sampling/logprob fields that Astra rejects are removed from the outbound body.
115.3/115.4 pin the inverse for the newly released Sol and Luna models. Both can disable reasoning, so none must survive; the requests include forced function calling because Chat tool use on these models depends on reasoning being disabled.
115.5 covers the GPT-6 max-effort ladder and the prompt-cache translation added for the family: cache_control becomes prompt_cache_breakpoint and opts the request into explicit cache mode.
115.6/115.7 are a real async-tool chain. The first response must return async on its function_call; the second replays that pending call without a tool output. Dropping async on replay makes OpenAI reject the request with "No tool output found for function call".
115.8 proves async is retained only on the supported function/custom tool kinds when they are mixed with another tool.

Every shaping assertion reads extra_fields.raw_request via x-bf-send-back-raw-request, so these rows verify what Bifrost sent rather than inferring it from a 2xx response.
